---
# [Bio181L_App_TE.qmd] ===============================================================================================================================
# Tiny Earth Public Database - BIO 181 Lab Analysis App (BYU-Idaho)
#
# This is a Quarto "Shiny document": a .qmd file whose `server: shiny`
# setting below turns it into a live web app. Every visitor gets their
# OWN independent session, so many students can use the app at the same
# time.
#
# HOW TO RUN LOCALLY (RStudio)
#   1. Install once (the same line is in Data_Pull.R and Data_Clean.R):
#        install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readxl", "httr2", "shiny", "DT", "car",
#                           "ggthemes", "scales", "writexl", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
#      (Quarto itself ships with recent RStudio versions.)
#   2. Open this file and click "Run Document" (or run
#        quarto::quarto_serve("Bio181L_App_TE.qmd")  in the Console).
#   3. The "Data" folder (made by the Data_Clean script) must sit in the
#      same folder as this file.
#
# HOW TO PUT IT ON THE WEB (so students only need a link)
#   A Shiny document needs a computer running R behind it, so it cannot
#   be hosted as a plain web page (e.g. GitHub Pages). Use a Shiny host
#   such as shinyapps.io (free tier available) or Posit Connect. From
#   RStudio, install `rsconnect`, link your shinyapps.io account, then
#   publish this file together with the whole "Data" folder.
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [MAP OF THIS FILE] =================================================================================================================================
# Press Ctrl+F / Cmd+F and search the tag, e.g. [D4]
#   [A] YAML settings (this block) ....... page title, layout, turns the document into a Shiny app
#   [B] STYLE SHEET (CSS) ................ colours, layout, buttons, tables, print rules
#         [B1] colour palette   [B2] banner   [B3] viewer layout   [B4] buttons
#         [B5] collapsible sections   [B6] variable picker   [B7] results page
#         [B8] data tables   [B9] print and small screens
#   [C] JAVASCRIPT ....................... tePick(): the Response / Explanatory checkboxes; teCsv(): table CSV downloads
#         [C2] KaTeX: draws the LaTeX equations in the test explanations
#   [D0] PACKAGES (R, runs once) ......... every library() the app uses, in its own chunk
#   [D] SETUP (R, runs once) ............. loading data, helpers, statistics
#         [D1] settings   [D2] find the tables   [D3] order and names
#         [D4] load and cache a table  [D5] variable descriptions
#         [D6] variable types and which test fits   [D7] formatting, table and graph helpers
#         [D8] DESIGNER SECTION: ANOVA, regression, chi-squared, logistic regression, test explanations
#         [D9] helpers that build pieces of the page (selector, picker, graph boxes and sizes)
#   [E] PAGE SHELL (R, built once) ....... banner + an empty "page" for the server to fill
#   [F] SERVER (R, runs for each visitor)  everything that reacts to clicks
#         [F1] app state   [F2] which page shows   [F3] left panel
#         [F4] picker status and Analyze button   [F5] right panel (tables)
#         [F6] click handlers   [F7] Background window   [F8] results page
#         [F9] Learn More window   [F10] Feedback window   [F11] Explore Data window and downloads   [F12] Debug windows   [F13] Worksheet window
#
# HOW A CLICK TRAVELS:  a button or link sends a value to R (input$...)  ->  an
# observeEvent() in [F6] updates the visitor's state rv$...  ->  every renderUI()
# that reads rv$... redraws itself  ->  the visitor sees the new screen.
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [A. YAML settings] =================================================================================================================================
# Page title, layout, and the line that turns this document into a
# Shiny app.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
pagetitle: "Tiny Earth Public Database - BIO 181 Lab Analysis App"  # page title shown in the browser tab
format:                   # output is an HTML page (a Shiny document = HTML page + a live R process)
  html:
    page-layout: custom   # no Quarto sidebar or margins; the app controls its own layout (see [B])
    toc: false            # no table of contents in the page
execute:                  # code chunks run, but their code, warnings and messages are hidden
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
server: shiny             # makes the document a live Shiny app (needs R running behind it)
---

```{=html}
<!-- [B. STYLE SHEET (CSS)] ==========================================================================================================================
     Clean, professional sea-green + cyan theme. All colours are defined
     once below so they are easy to change.
     ============================================================================================================================================= -->
<style>
  /* [B1. Colour palette] ============================================================================================================================
     Each colour is defined once here and used below as var(--name).
     Change a colour here and it changes everywhere.
       body                           page background and default text
                                      colour
       #quarto-content, main.content  remove Quarto's default page-width
                                      limit so the app uses the whole
                                      window
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  :root {
    --sea:        #2E8B57;   /* sea green (primary)            */
    --sea-dark:   #1B5E4B;   /* deep sea green (headings)      */
    --cyan:       #00ACC1;   /* cyan (secondary)               */
    --cyan-light: #E0F7FA;   /* pale cyan (backgrounds)        */
    --mint:       #EAF6F0;   /* pale sea green (backgrounds)   */
    --grey:       #5F7470;
  }
  body                 { background: #F4FAF8; color: #25403A; }
  #quarto-content, main.content { max-width: 100% !important; padding: 0 14px 20px 14px !important; }

  /* [B2. Banner at the very top] ====================================================================================================================
       .te-banner     green-to-cyan gradient bar across the top of the
                      page
       .te-banner h1  banner title
       .te-banner p   the line of text under the title
       .te-banner-art the zoomed-in bacteria drawing on the far right of
                      the banner, cut off at the banner's edges; its
                      left edge fades out and is gone by the 4/5 point
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  html, body { overflow-x: clip; }  /* the banner's negative side margins would otherwise add a sideways scrollbar */
  .te-banner { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sea), var(--cyan)); color: #fff; position: relative; overflow: hidden;
               padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 0 0 12px 12px; margin: 0 -14px 14px -14px; }
  .te-banner h1 { font-size: 1.45rem; margin: 0; font-weight: 700; color: #fff; position: relative; }
  .te-banner p  { margin: 2px 0 0 0; opacity: .92; font-size: .9rem; position: relative; }
  .te-banner-art { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; right: 0; left: 80%; pointer-events: none;   /* left: where the fade ends */
                   -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(0,0,0,.45) 45%, #000 85%);
                           mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(0,0,0,.45) 45%, #000 85%); }
  .te-banner-art svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block; }

  /* [B3. Viewer layout: selector (left) + table (right)] ============================================================================================
       .app-grid         two-column grid: a 310px selector on the left,
                         the table fills the rest on the right
       .panel-card       the white rounded 'card' that every panel sits on
       .left-col         left grid cell; the right card sets the row's
                         height, so both cards end at the same line
       .left-card        left card: fills .left-col exactly, children
                         stacked top-to-bottom so the buttons stay at the
                         bottom
       .selector-scroll  middle of the left card: takes the spare space
                         and scrolls when the list is long
       .sel-title        bold heading at the top of a panel
       .sel-head         small uppercase section heading (Individual /
                         Combined)
       .te-item          one clickable table name in the selector;
                         .active marks the selected table
       .hint             small grey helper text
       .vtype            small grey '(Quantitative)' tag shown after a
                         variable name
       .viewer-head      title row (bold) above the Table Viewer /
                         Variable Description
       .table-foot       line of text under the table (row and column
                         counts)
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  .app-grid  { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 310px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 14px; }
  .panel-card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #CDE7DF; border-radius: 10px; padding: 14px;
                box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(27,94,75,.08); }
  .left-col   { position: relative; min-height: 60vh; }
  .left-card  { display: flex; flex-direction: column; position: absolute; inset: 0; }
  .selector-scroll { flex: 1 1 auto; overflow-y: auto; margin: 10px 0; padding-right: 4px; }
  .sel-title  { font-weight: 700; color: var(--sea-dark); font-size: 1.05rem; margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .sel-head   { font-size: .75rem; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 700;
                color: var(--cyan); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); margin: 12px 0 4px; padding-bottom: 2px; }
  .te-item    { display: block; padding: 5px 10px; margin: 1px 0; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--sea-dark);
                text-decoration: none !important; font-size: .93rem; }
  .te-item:hover  { background: var(--cyan-light); }
  .te-item.active { background: var(--sea); color: #fff !important; font-weight: 600; }
  .hint       { color: var(--grey); font-size: .88rem; margin: 2px 0 6px; }
  .vtype      { color: var(--grey); font-size: .8rem; margin-left: 6px; }
  .viewer-head { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline;
                 border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); margin-bottom: 10px; padding-bottom: 4px; }
  .viewer-head h3 { margin: 0; color: var(--sea-dark); font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 700; }
  .viewer-head .current { color: var(--grey); font-size: .9rem; }
  .table-foot { color: var(--grey); font-size: .85rem; margin-top: 6px; }

  /* [B4. Buttons] ===================================================================================================================================
       .btn-te            main green button style; every button in the
                          app starts from this
       .btn-cyan          cyan variant of the button
       .btn-outline       white outlined variant, used for secondary
                          actions (Back, Description)
       .btn-wide          makes a button fill the full width of its panel
       .btn-te[disabled]  greyed-out look for a disabled button (Analyze
                          before a valid pair is chosen)
       .btn-glow          glowing cyan look for the Analyze button once a
                          valid pair is chosen; only the glow pulses
                          gently (te-pulse), the button itself stays still
       .btn-row           a row of buttons that share the width evenly
                          (Description + Run Analysis, Back + Analyze)
       .btn-round         round icon-only button (Worksheet, Explore Data
                          and Feedback on the results page)
       .has-tip           a styled hover label (bigger and brighter than
                          the browser's own tooltip) that reads the
                          button's data-tip text; used on the round
                          buttons and the Debug button
       .btn-square        small square icon-only button (the Debug bug)
       .debug-corner      pins the Debug button to the bottom-left corner
                          of the screen
       .tip-start         hover label that opens to the right and wraps
                          (for a button at the left edge)
       .dl-choice         the Raw / Clean choice cards in the Explore
                          Data window
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  .btn-te        { background: var(--sea); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--sea); border-radius: 8px;
                   font-weight: 600; padding: 7px 16px; }
  .btn-te:hover  { background: #247549; color: #fff; }
  .btn-cyan      { background: var(--cyan); border-color: var(--cyan); }
  .btn-cyan:hover{ background: #0090a3; }
  .btn-outline   { background: #fff; color: var(--sea-dark); border: 1px solid var(--sea); }
  .btn-outline:hover { background: var(--mint); color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .btn-wide      { width: 100%; }
  .btn-te[disabled] { background: #D5DFDC; border-color: #D5DFDC; color: #8A9A96; cursor: not-allowed; }
  .btn-glow      { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,172,193,.25), 0 0 14px rgba(0,172,193,.85);
                   background: var(--cyan); border-color: var(--cyan); animation: te-pulse 1.8s ease-in-out infinite; }
  @keyframes te-pulse {
    0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,172,193,.25), 0 0 10px rgba(0,172,193,.6); }
    50%      { box-shadow: 0 0 0 6px rgba(0,172,193,.18), 0 0 20px rgba(0,172,193,.95); }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .btn-glow { animation: none; } }
  .btn-row       { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; }
  .btn-row .btn  { flex: 1; }
  .btn-row > *   { flex: 1; }                 /* Back and Analyze share the row evenly */
  .btn-row .shiny-html-output .btn { width: 100%; }
  .btn-round     { width: 42px; height: 42px; padding: 0; border-radius: 50%; font-size: 1.05rem;
                   display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
  .btn-square    { width: 34px; height: 34px; padding: 0; flex: none; font-size: 1rem;
                   display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
  .has-tip       { position: relative; }
  .has-tip::after { content: attr(data-tip); position: absolute; top: calc(100% + 10px); right: 0; z-index: 20;
                   background: var(--cyan); color: #fff; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap;
                   padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0,172,193,.45);
                   opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-4px); pointer-events: none; transition: opacity .2s ease, transform .2s ease; }
  .has-tip:hover::after, .has-tip:focus-visible::after { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  .tip-start::after { left: 0; right: auto; width: 270px; white-space: normal; }  /* label opens to the right (button at a left edge) and wraps */
  .debug-corner  { position: fixed; left: 12px; bottom: 12px; z-index: 30; }      /* Debug button: bottom-left corner of the screen */
  .debug-corner::after { top: auto; bottom: calc(100% + 10px); }                   /* its label opens upward */
  .has-tip:disabled { pointer-events: auto; cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 1;
                      background: #CFD8DC; border-color: #CFD8DC; color: #fff; }  /* Bootstrap blocks hover on disabled buttons; keep the label */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .has-tip::after { transition: none; } }
  .dl-choices    { display: flex; gap: 12px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .dl-choice     { flex: 1 1 200px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 10px;
                   border: 1px solid var(--sea); background: #fff; color: var(--sea-dark); text-decoration: none; }
  .dl-choice:hover { background: var(--mint); color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .dl-choice strong { font-size: 1.05rem; }
  .dl-choice span { font-size: .88rem; color: #4A5A56; }

  /* [B5. Collapsible selector sections (<details> / <summary>)] =====================================================================================
     The heading is clickable; the browser's default triangle is hidden.
     We draw our own arrow instead; it turns 90 degrees when the section
     is open.
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head { cursor: pointer; list-style: none; }
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head::before { content: "\25B8"; display: inline-block; width: 1em;
                                                    transition: transform .15s; }
  details.sel-details[open] > summary.sel-head::before { transform: rotate(90deg); }

  /* [B6. Variable picker: name + Response box + Explanatory box] ====================================================================================
       .pick-head, .pick-row  header and every row share one 3-column
                              grid (name, Response, Explanatory) so the
                              checkboxes line up
       .pick-head             column headings stay visible (sticky)
                              while the variable list scrolls underneath
       .pick-row              one variable row in the picker (highlights
                              on hover)
       input.pick-resp        Response checkboxes are sea green
       input.pick-expl        Explanatory checkboxes are cyan
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  .pick-head, .pick-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 64px 64px; gap: 4px; align-items: center; }
  .pick-head  { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1; background: #fff; padding: 2px 4px 5px;
                border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; }
  .pick-head span:first-child { text-align: left; color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .pick-head .h-resp { color: var(--sea); }
  .pick-head .h-expl { color: var(--cyan); }
  .pick-row   { padding: 3px 4px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: .93rem; }
  .pick-row:hover { background: var(--cyan-light); }
  .pick-name  { overflow-wrap: anywhere; color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .pick-row input { justify-self: center; width: 17px; height: 17px; cursor: pointer; }
  .pick-row input.pick-resp { accent-color: var(--sea); }
  .pick-row input.pick-expl { accent-color: var(--cyan); }

  /* [B7. Results page] ==============================================================================================================================
       .results-page           the results page itself: no card border, it
                               fills the screen under the banner
       .results-bar            top bar of the results page (Back on the
                               left; Learn More, Save PDF and the round
                               buttons on the right)
       .results-page h2        test title at the top of the results
       .sec-title              section headings on the results page
                               (Graphical Summary, Numerical Summary, ...)
       .tbl-wrap               wrapper that lets a wide table scroll
                               sideways instead of stretching the page
       .tbl-cap                bold caption above a table
       .te-table               style for the summary and test tables
                               built by html_table()
       .learn                  the Learn More window: its table fills the
                               width and long cells wrap
       .formula                shaded boxes used for equations and
                               hypotheses
       .formula-note           pale blue box under each equation that
                               explains its symbols
       .concl                  cyan box for written conclusions and
                               warnings
       .note                   small italic grey notes
       ...validation           friendly box for the message shown when a
                               test cannot run (replaces Shiny's faint
                               grey text)
       .more-toggle            space above the View More on Test button
       .more-body              the test details are hidden until the
                               button adds the class 'open' to .more
       .diag-row               diagnostic plots sit side by side and wrap
                               onto a new line when the window is narrow
       .diag-title             heading over a group of diagnostic plots
                               (regression: original model / log model)
       details.contrasts       collapsible box for the Tukey contrasts
       .shiny-plot-output img  never let a plot be wider than the page
       .dl-box                 a graph plus its download icon (built by
                               plot_box()); the box is as wide as the graph
       .dl-menu                the download icon in the graph's top-right
                               corner; clicking it opens PDF / PNG links
       .csv-btn                "CSV" download button beside a table's
                               caption; only shown inside .csv-tables (the
                               Numerical Summary). To offer CSV on every
                               table, delete the "display: none" rule.
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  .results-bar  { display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 8px; }
  .results-bar .spacer { flex: 1; }
  .results-page h2   { color: var(--sea-dark); margin: 6px 0 2px; }
  .panel-card.results-page { border: 0; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none; margin: -14px -14px -20px; padding: 16px 22px 28px;
                             min-height: calc(100vh - 70px); }  /* one white page under the banner, edge to edge, lined up with the banner text */
  .sec-title    { color: var(--sea-dark); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); padding-bottom: 3px;
                  margin: 22px 0 10px; font-size: 1.15rem; }
  .tbl-wrap     { overflow-x: auto; margin: 6px 0 14px; }
  .tbl-cap      { font-weight: 600; color: var(--sea-dark); margin-bottom: 3px; font-size: .92rem; }
  .te-table     { border-collapse: collapse; font-size: .88rem; min-width: 40%; }
  .te-table th  { background: var(--cyan-light); color: var(--sea-dark); padding: 5px 10px; text-align: left;
                  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan); white-space: nowrap; }
  .te-table td  { padding: 4px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid #E1EEEA; white-space: nowrap; }
  .te-table tr:nth-child(even) td { background: #F7FBFA; }
  .learn .te-table    { width: 100%; }
  .learn .te-table td { white-space: normal; }  /* let long cells wrap inside the Learn More window */
  .learn li           { margin-bottom: 4px; }
  .formula      { background: var(--mint); border-left: 4px solid var(--sea); padding: 8px 12px; margin: 4px 0;
                  border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; overflow-x: auto; }  /* math is drawn by KaTeX (see [C2]) */
  .formula .katex { font-size: 1.12em; }
  .concl        { background: var(--cyan-light); border-left: 4px solid var(--cyan); padding: 8px 12px;
                  border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; }
  .note         { color: var(--grey); font-size: .85rem; font-style: italic; }
  .results-page .shiny-output-error-validation { color: var(--sea-dark); background: var(--cyan-light);
                  border-left: 4px solid var(--cyan); padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0;
                  font-size: .95rem; margin: 10px 0; }
  .more-toggle  { margin-top: 22px; }
  .more-body    { display: none; }
  .more.open .more-body { display: block; }
  .diag-row     { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px; }
  .diag-title   { color: var(--sea-dark); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 14px 0 6px; }
  details.contrasts { margin: 6px 0 14px; border: 1px solid var(--cyan-light); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; }
  details.contrasts > summary { cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; color: var(--sea-dark); }
  details.contrasts[open] > summary { margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .formula-note { background: #EAF6FB; border-left: 4px solid #8FCFE0; padding: 6px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0;
                  font-size: .9rem; color: #2F5560; }
  .shiny-plot-output img { max-width: 100%; height: auto !important; }
  .dl-box       { position: relative; width: fit-content; max-width: 100%; }
  .dl-menu      { position: absolute; top: 6px; right: 6px; z-index: 2; text-align: right; }
  .dl-menu > summary { list-style: none; cursor: pointer; display: inline-block; background: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
                  color: var(--sea-dark); border: 1px solid var(--sea); border-radius: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; }
  .dl-menu > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
  .dl-menu > summary:hover, .dl-menu[open] > summary { background: var(--mint); }
  .dl-menu a    { display: block; margin-top: 3px; padding: 3px 14px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--cyan);
                  border-radius: 6px; color: var(--sea-dark); font-weight: 600; font-size: .85rem; text-decoration: none; }
  .dl-menu a:hover { background: var(--cyan-light); }
  .csv-btn      { display: none; }
  .csv-tables .csv-btn { display: inline-block; margin-left: 8px; padding: 0 7px; font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 600;
                  color: var(--sea-dark); background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--sea); border-radius: 6px; }
  .csv-tables .csv-btn:hover { background: var(--mint); }

  /* [B8. DataTable touches] =========================================================================================================================
       table.dataTable thead th  cyan header cells in the data tables
       table.dataTable th, td    every header and cell left-aligned (DT
                                 right-aligns number columns by default)
                                 and kept on one line (no text wrapping;
                                 the table scrolls sideways instead)
       .paginate_button.current  green highlight on the current page
                                 button of a data table
       .dataTables_filter input  the Search box, trimmed to the same 34px
                                 height as the "Show [n] entries" drop-down
       .dataTables_length,       an 8px gap between those two controls and
       .dataTables_filter        the table below them
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  table.dataTable thead th { background: var(--cyan-light); color: var(--sea-dark); }
  table.dataTable th, table.dataTable td { text-align: left !important; white-space: nowrap; }
  .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_paginate .paginate_button.current { background: var(--sea) !important;
        color: #fff !important; border: 1px solid var(--sea) !important; }
  .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_filter input { box-sizing: border-box; height: 34px; padding: 2px 6px; }
  .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_length, .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_filter { margin-bottom: 8px; }

  /* [B9. Print ("Save PDF") and small-screen rules] =================================================================================================
     Printing: hide anything marked no-print (buttons) and pop-up
     notifications, always show the test details, use a plain white
     page, and keep the banner colours.
     Narrow screens (phones): stack the selector above the table and let
     the card grow.
     ============================================================================================================================================== */
  @media print {
    .no-print  { display: none !important; }                                      /* hide buttons */
    .more-body { display: block !important; }                                     /* show details */
    body       { background: #fff; }                                              /* white page */
    .te-banner { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }  /* keep colours */
    .shiny-notification-panel { display: none !important; }                       /* hide pop-ups */
  }
  @media (max-width: 900px) { .app-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .left-col { min-height: 0; }
                              .left-card { position: static; height: auto; } }
</style>

<!-- [C. JAVASCRIPT] =================================================================================================================================
     Two small functions: tePick() controls the Response / Explanatory
     checkboxes in the variable picker, and teCsv() downloads a results
     table as a CSV file.
     ============================================================================================================================================= -->
<script>
  // [tePick()] ======================================================================================================================================
  // Called by every checkbox in the variable picker (see pick_row() in
  // the setup code).
  //  - only ONE box may be ticked in each column (Response / Explanatory)
  //  - one variable cannot be both Response and Explanatory
  // It then tells the server which variable is in each column
  // (input$sel_pair).
  // =================================================================================================================================================
  function tePick(col, box) {
    var other = (col === 'resp') ? 'expl' : 'resp';  // the opposite column to this box's column
    // -- Untick --
    // Untick every other box in this column, so only one is ticked per
    // column. If this variable is ticked in the other column too, untick
    // it there (a variable cannot be both).
    document.querySelectorAll('input.pick-' + col).forEach(function (b) { if (b !== box) b.checked = false; });
    if (box.checked) {
      document.querySelectorAll('input.pick-' + other).forEach(function (b) {
        if (b.dataset.v === box.dataset.v) b.checked = false;
      });
    }
    var chosen = function (c) {  // the variable ticked in column c, or '' if none is ticked
      var b = document.querySelector('input.pick-' + c + ':checked');
      return b ? b.dataset.v : '';
    };
    // -- Send both choices to R --
    // The server receives them as input$sel_pair$resp and
    // input$sel_pair$expl.
    Shiny.setInputValue('sel_pair', { resp: chosen('resp'), expl: chosen('expl') }, { priority: 'event' });
  }

  // [teCsv()] =======================================================================================================================================
  // Called by a table's "CSV" button (see html_table() in the setup
  // code). Copies the table on the page, header row first, into a CSV
  // file and downloads it. Every cell is wrapped in quotes so commas in
  // numbers such as 1,234 stay in one cell. The ﻿ mark at the start
  // tells Excel the file is UTF-8, so symbols show correctly.
  // =================================================================================================================================================
  function teCsv(btn) {
    var wrap = btn.closest('.tbl-wrap');
    var rows = Array.from(wrap.querySelectorAll('tr')).map(function (tr) {
      return Array.from(tr.children).map(function (cell) {
        return '"' + cell.textContent.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"';
      }).join(',');
    });
    var link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(['﻿' + rows.join('\r\n')], { type: 'text/csv' }));
    link.download = btn.dataset.name + '.csv';
    link.click();
    URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href);
  }
</script>

<!-- [C2. LaTeX math (KaTeX)] ========================================================================================================================
     KaTeX draws the LaTeX in the test explanations (text between \( and
     \) in test_info) as real math: fractions stacked, exponents raised.
     Shiny adds the results page after the page loads, so a watcher
     re-draws the math whenever new content appears. Without internet the
     equations stay readable as plain LaTeX text.
     ============================================================================================================================================= -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.11/dist/katex.min.css">
<script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.11/dist/katex.min.js"></script>
<script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.11/dist/contrib/auto-render.min.js"></script>
<script>
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    var timer = null;
    var draw = function () {
      if (!window.renderMathInElement) return;
      document.querySelectorAll('.formula, .formula-note').forEach(function (el) {
        if (el.dataset.math) return;  // already drawn
        renderMathInElement(el, { delimiters: [{ left: '\\(', right: '\\)', display: false }], throwOnError: false });
        el.dataset.math = '1';
      });
    };
    new MutationObserver(function () { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(draw, 100); })
      .observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    window.addEventListener('load', draw);
  });
</script>
```

```{r}
#| context: setup
# [D0. PACKAGES] =====================================================================================================================================
# Every package the app uses, loaded in one place. "context: setup" makes these available to the whole app, including the server part that runs for
# each visitor.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
library(tidyverse)  # ggplot2 (graphs), readr (read_csv() for data_dictionary.csv), and more
library(shiny)      # the web-app framework
library(DT)         # interactive, filterable data tables
# car (Levene's test), ggthemes (theme_economist), scales (axis labels) and writexl (Clean Data downloads as .xlsx) must be installed too. They are
# called with :: (e.g. car::leveneTest()) instead of loaded with library(), because loading car would hide dplyr's recode() and purrr's some().
```

```{r}
#| context: setup
# [D. SETUP] =========================================================================================================================================
# Runs once when the app starts (shared by all users). Finds the cleaned .rds files and defines every helper function the app needs. (The packages are
# loaded just above, in [D0].)
# ====================================================================================================================================================

  # [D1. Settings] ===================================================================================================================================
  # Search for [D1]...[D9] to jump between the parts of this setup section.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
DATA_DIR   <- "Data"   # folder holding the cleaned .rds files
MAX_LEVELS <- 30       # text variables with MORE distinct values are hidden from the picker
TOP_LEVELS <- 10       # analyses keep the 10 most common groups; the rest become "Other"
ALPHA      <- 0.05     # significance level used in the written conclusions
QQ_OUTSIDE <- 0.10     # residuals count as "not normal" when more than this share fall outside the Q-Q plot's 95% band (see qq_check())
GRAPH_STYLE <- "economist"  # graph look: "economist" (ggthemes::theme_economist, blue-grey panel) or "minimal" (plain white); see te_theme()
FEEDBACK_URL <- "https://forms.gle/rF1p59ydqe97piHw5"  # feedback form opened by the round speech-bubble button on the results page [F10]

  # [Analysis worksheets] ============================================================================================================================
  # The round microscope button on the results page is for downloadable analysis worksheets [F13]. While WORKSHEET_ENABLED is FALSE the button is
  # shown greyed out and does nothing. To turn it on: put the files in the WORKSHEET_DIR folder, named <test>_worksheet.docx and/or
  # <test>_worksheet.pdf, where <test> is anova, regression, chisq or logistic (e.g. "Worksheets/anova_worksheet.docx"), then set it to TRUE.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
WORKSHEET_ENABLED <- FALSE
WORKSHEET_DIR     <- "Worksheets"

  # [Debug mode] =====================================================================================================================================
  # DEBUG_MODE = TRUE shows a square bug button in the bottom-left corner of the main screen [F12]. It opens each test's results page in its own
  # window (the URL ends in ?debug=<test>), so layouts can be checked without picking variables. Set it to FALSE before publishing the app for students.
  # DEBUG_CASES: one analysis per test, chosen to show as much of each layout as possible:
  #   anova       11 soil types: long Tukey table, and the residuals fail the Q-Q check so Kruskal-Wallis appears
  #   regression  CFU/g is very skewed, so the automatic log(y) refit and all four diagnostic plots appear
  #   chisq       11 soil types x 4 activity results: many graph panels, and small expected counts add the Monte Carlo p-value
  #   logistic    a significant result with Inconclusive rows left out (the note under the summary appears)
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
DEBUG_MODE  <- TRUE
DEBUG_CASES <- list(
  anova      = list(table = "samples_combined",            resp = "sample_ph",             expl = "soil_type"),
  regression = list(table = "dilutions_combined",          resp = "cfug",                  expl = "sample_ph"),
  chisq      = list(table = "aa_screen_isolates_combined", resp = "antibiotic_activity",   expl = "sample_soil_type"),
  logistic   = list(table = "eukaryotics_combined",        resp = "eukaryotic_inhibition", expl = "temperature"))

  # [D2. Find the cleaned tables] ====================================================================================================================
  # Every .rds in Data/ is one table. Files ending in "_combined" are the "Combined" tables; everything else is "Individual". (data_dictionary.csv is
  # not an .rds, so it is never mistaken for a table.)
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
rds_files       <- list.files(DATA_DIR, pattern = "\\.rds$")
all_keys        <- str_remove(rds_files, "\\.rds$")
combined_keys   <- str_subset(all_keys, "_combined$")
individual_keys <- setdiff(all_keys, combined_keys)

  # [D3. Table order and display names] ==============================================================================================================
  # Show tables in the same order as the Tiny Earth database; anything not in this list is placed at the end (alphabetical).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
preferred_order <- c("institutions", "samples", "dilutions", "library_collections",
                     "aa_screen_libraries", "isolates", "streaks", "aa_screen_isolates",
                     "gram_stains", "other_tests", "rrna_analyses", "antibio_suscepts",
                     "eukaryotics", "extracts", "aa_screen_extracts")

  # [sort_keys()] ====================================================================================================================================
  # Puts table names in the preferred order; tables not in the list go last, alphabetically. '_combined' is dropped first so a combined table sorts
  # right beside its individual version. match() = position in preferred_order; nomatch = 99 sends unknown tables to the end.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
sort_keys <- function(keys) {
  base <- str_remove(keys, "_combined$")
  keys[order(match(base, preferred_order, nomatch = 99L), keys)]
}
individual_keys <- sort_keys(individual_keys)  # apply the ordering to both groups of tables
combined_keys   <- sort_keys(combined_keys)

  # [pretty_name()] ==================================================================================================================================
  # "antibio_suscepts_combined" -> "Antibio Suscepts" (label shown to students). Acronyms are then fixed by hand: "Aa" -> "AA" (antibiotic
  # activity) and "Rrna" -> "rRNA".
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
pretty_name <- function(key) {
  tools::toTitleCase(str_replace_all(str_remove(key, "_combined$"), "_", " ")) %>%
    str_replace_all(c("\\bAa\\b" = "AA", "\\bRrna\\b" = "rRNA"))
}

  # [D4. Load a table (once), then remember it] ======================================================================================================
  # `table_cache` is shared by all users, so each file is read from disk only the first time anyone opens it. read_rds() returns the table exactly as
  # Data_Clean saved it, with every column type intact.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
table_cache <- new.env()  # acts like a shared lookup list: name of table -> data frame
load_table <- function(key) {  # load_table('isolates') returns that table, reading its file once
  if (!exists(key, envir = table_cache, inherits = FALSE)) {  # not cached yet? read it from disk
    path <- file.path(DATA_DIR, paste0(key, ".rds"))
    df   <- read_rds(path)                               # read the table, types intact
    assign(key, as.data.frame(df), envir = table_cache)  # plain data.frame: what DT/stats expect
  }
  get(key, envir = table_cache, inherits = FALSE)  # return the cached copy
}

  # [D5. Variable descriptions (the "Description" view)] =============================================================================================
  # OPTIONAL file: Data/data_dictionary.csv with 3 columns:
  #   table, variable, description
  # One row per column of each Individual table (Combined tables reuse these rows, see lookup_description()). A blank description shows the "not yet
  # documented" reminder. Whatever you write there is shown in the Variable Description. We start with an empty dictionary so the app still works when
  # the file is missing.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
dictionary <- tibble(table = character(), variable = character(), description = character())
dict_path  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "data_dictionary.csv")
if (file.exists(dict_path)) {  # if the file exists, read it with every column as text ('c')
  dictionary <- read_csv(dict_path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"), progress = FALSE)
}

  # [lookup_description()] ===========================================================================================================================
  # Finds the description for one variable. Order of search:
  #   Rule 1. same table + same variable name
  #   Rule 2. same variable name in any table
  #   Rule 3. columns joined in from another table carry that table's prefix ("sample_", "isolate_", "institution_"), so look them up in that table
  #           without the prefix (e.g. isolate_date -> isolates / date). `joined` lists the prefixes.
  # Nothing found: show a reminder instead of a blank. Dictionary entries use the plain table name, so '_combined' is dropped first.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
lookup_description <- function(key, var) {
  tbl  <- str_remove(key, "_combined$")
  # -- pick() --
  # The first non-blank description in a vector, or NA if there is none.
  pick <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d) & nzchar(d)]; if (length(d)) d[1] else NA_character_ }
  out  <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$table == tbl & dictionary$variable == var])
  if (is.na(out)) out <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$variable == var])
  joined <- c(sample_ = "samples", isolate_ = "isolates", institution_ = "institutions")  # prefix -> table it came from
  for (p in names(joined)) if (is.na(out) && str_starts(var, p))
    out <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$table == joined[[p]] & dictionary$variable == str_remove(var, fixed(p))])
  if (is.na(out)) "(not yet documented - add it to Data/data_dictionary.csv)" else out
}

  # [D6. Variable types and test choice] =============================================================================================================
  # Quantitative = numbers. Qualitative = categories (text or TRUE/FALSE). These two types decide which test is run. In var_type(), dates are excluded
  # from analysis; numbers (including counts) are Quantitative; everything else (text, TRUE/FALSE) is Qualitative.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
var_type <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXct"))) "Date"
  else if (is.numeric(x))                "Quantitative"
  else                                   "Qualitative"
}

  # [binary_outcome()] ===============================================================================================================================
  # Can a qualitative response be used in logistic regression? "Inconclusive" and "Isolate did not grow" are not real outcomes, so they are set to NA
  # first. If exactly two outcomes are left, returns list(y = the cleaned values as text, event = the outcome being modelled, other = the other one);
  # otherwise NULL. The event is "Yes" or "TRUE" when present, else the second outcome alphabetically (what glm() would model).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
binary_outcome <- function(x) {
  x  <- as.character(x)
  x[str_detect(str_to_lower(x), "inconclusive|did not grow")] <- NA
  lv <- sort(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
  if (length(lv) != 2) return(NULL)
  event <- if ("Yes" %in% lv) "Yes" else if ("TRUE" %in% lv) "TRUE" else lv[2]
  list(y = x, event = event, other = setdiff(lv, event))
}

  # [pick_test()] ====================================================================================================================================
  # Which of the four tests fits a Response / Explanatory pair? resp and expl are the two columns themselves.
  #   quantitative response + qualitative explanatory   -> ANOVA
  #   quantitative response + quantitative explanatory  -> simple linear regression
  #   qualitative  response + qualitative  explanatory  -> chi-squared test
  #   qualitative  response + quantitative explanatory  -> logistic regression, but only if the response has exactly two outcomes (binary_outcome())
  # Anything else returns NA.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
pick_test <- function(resp, expl) {
  resp_type <- var_type(resp); expl_type <- var_type(expl)
  if      (resp_type == "Quantitative" && expl_type == "Qualitative")  "anova"
  else if (resp_type == "Quantitative" && expl_type == "Quantitative") "regression"
  else if (resp_type == "Qualitative"  && expl_type == "Qualitative")  "chisq"
  else if (resp_type == "Qualitative"  && expl_type == "Quantitative" && !is.null(binary_outcome(resp))) "logistic"
  else NA_character_
}

  # [describe_type()] ================================================================================================================================
  # A more detailed label, used only in the Type column of the Variable Description. ID columns only link tables together, so they are labelled that way
  # to stop students analysing them. Text with a huge number of different values is flagged (the picker hides these).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
describe_type <- function(name, x) {
  if (name == "id" || str_detect(name, "_id$")) return("ID (row link)")
  t <- var_type(x)
  if (t == "Qualitative" && n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE) > MAX_LEVELS) return("Text (many values)")
  t
}

  # [analysis_vars()] ================================================================================================================================
  # Which columns of a table are sensible to analyse? We drop ID columns, dates, constant columns, and text columns with too many different values (a
  # chi-squared table with hundreds of rows is unreadable).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analysis_vars <- function(df) {
  keep <- map_lgl(names(df), function(v) {  # one TRUE/FALSE per column: offer it in the picker?
    x <- df[[v]]
    if (v == "id" || str_detect(v, "_id$")) return(FALSE)       # drop ID columns
    if (var_type(x) == "Date")              return(FALSE)       # drop dates
    n_unique <- n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE)                     # distinct non-missing values
    if (n_unique < 2)                       return(FALSE)       # 0 or 1 values: nothing to compare
    if (!is.numeric(x) && n_unique > MAX_LEVELS) return(FALSE)  # text with too many categories
    TRUE
  })
  names(df)[keep]  # the names of the columns that were kept
}

  # [lump_levels()] ==================================================================================================================================
  # Keeps the TOP_LEVELS most common categories and lumps the rest into "Other".
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
lump_levels <- function(x, top = TOP_LEVELS) {
  x      <- as.character(x)                    # text, so all value types behave the same
  counts <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)  # count each category, most common first
  if (length(counts) > top) {                  # only lump when there are more than the limit
    keep <- names(counts)[seq_len(top)]       # the names of the most common categories
    x[!is.na(x) & !(x %in% keep)] <- "Other"  # everything else -> 'Other' (NA stays NA)
  }
  factor(x)  # return a factor (R's type for categories)
}

  # [D7. Formatting, table and graph helpers] ========================================================================================================
  # fmt_p()  a p-value as text: blank if missing, '< 0.0001' if tiny, otherwise 4 decimals
  # fmt_n()  a number as text with d decimals (default 3)
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
fmt_p <- function(p) case_when(is.na(p)    ~ "",
                               p < 0.0001  ~ "< 0.0001",
                               .default    = formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 4))
fmt_n <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)

  # [html_table()] ===================================================================================================================================
  # Turns a data.frame into a tidy HTML table (used in the results page). fmt_col() formats one column: numbers are rounded to 3 decimals with
  # thousands commas and NA shown blank; anything else is shown as text. The HTML is an optional caption, then a <table> with a header row and one row
  # per data row. The caption also holds a "CSV" button that calls teCsv() (JavaScript [C]); data-name is the file name, made from the caption. The
  # button is only visible in the Numerical Summary (see .csv-btn in [B7]).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
html_table <- function(df, caption = NULL) {
  fmt_col <- function(col) {
    if (is.numeric(col)) {
      out <- format(round(col, 3), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")
      out[is.na(col)] <- ""
    } else {
      out <- as.character(col); out[is.na(out)] <- ""
    }
    out
  }
  df[] <- lapply(df, fmt_col)  # apply fmt_col to every column (df[] keeps the data.frame shape)
  tags$div(class = "tbl-wrap",
    if (!is.null(caption)) tags$div(class = "tbl-cap", caption,
      tags$button(type = "button", class = "csv-btn no-print", title = "Download this table as a CSV file (opens in Excel)",
                  `data-name` = str_replace_all(caption, "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"), onclick = "teCsv(this);", icon("download"), "CSV")),
    tags$table(class = "te-table",
      tags$thead(tags$tr(lapply(names(df), tags$th))),
      tags$tbody(lapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) tags$tr(lapply(df[i, ], tags$td))))))
}

  # [var_label()] ====================================================================================================================================
  # A column name as graph text: underscores become spaces and words are capitalized ("sample_ph" -> "Sample pH"). Abbreviations are fixed by hand.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
var_label <- function(v) {
  tools::toTitleCase(str_replace_all(v, "_", " ")) %>%
    str_replace_all(c("\\bPh\\b" = "pH", "\\bCfug\\b" = "CFU/g", "\\bLat\\b" = "Latitude", "\\bLng\\b" = "Longitude",
                      "\\bAa\\b" = "AA", "\\bRrna\\b" = "rRNA"))
}

  # [Graph theme + green -> cyan colour ramp] ========================================================================================================
  # te_cols(n)  n colours for groups in graphs. Up to 3 groups blend sea green to cyan. More groups use a wider, still muted ramp (deep green ->
  #             soft green -> teal -> pale cyan -> slate blue) and alternate its two halves, so neighbouring bars and boxes never get near-identical
  #             colours.
  # te_theme()  the common graph look, chosen by GRAPH_STYLE [D1]: The Economist's style (ggthemes) or a plain white one; both get a bold green
  #             title
  # y_axis(), x_axis()  number axes with evenly spaced "pretty" breaks, short labels for big numbers (100M instead of 1e+08), and only a little
  #             padding past the data, so the data fill the graph
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
te_cols <- function(n) {
  n <- max(n, 1)
  if (n <= 3) return(grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#2E8B57", "#20B2AA", "#00BCD4"))(n))
  cols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#1B5E4B", "#2E8B57", "#7CBF97", "#20B2AA", "#8AD5D0", "#00A5B8", "#4D8597"))(n)
  cols[c(seq(1, n, 2), seq(2, n, 2))]  # 1, 3, 5, ... then 2, 4, 6, ...
}
te_theme <- function() {
  base <- if (GRAPH_STYLE == "economist") ggthemes::theme_economist(base_size = 11) else theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
  base +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1B5E4B"),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right",
          axis.ticks.length = unit(2, "pt"),                               # short ticks so the axis values sit close to the graph...
          axis.text.x  = element_text(margin = margin(t = 1)),
          axis.text.y  = element_text(margin = margin(r = 1)),
          axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),             # ...and the axis titles sit further away from the values
          axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
}
short_num <- scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())  # 0, 100M, 200M ...; 6.0, 6.5, 7.0 ...
y_axis <- function(n = 6, pad = c(.02, .05), ...) scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n), labels = short_num, expand = expansion(mult = pad), ...)
x_axis <- function(n = 8, ...) scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n), labels = short_num, expand = expansion(mult = .02), ...)

  # [Auto-sizing graph text] =========================================================================================================================
  # Graphs have a fixed width (PLOT_W [D9]), so long or numerous labels must shrink or wrap instead of overlapping.
  # fit_size(n, at)  text size for n labels: full size (10) for up to `at` labels, then smaller in proportion, but never below 8
  # wrap_at(width)   a labeller that breaks text longer than `width` characters onto extra lines (used for axis labels, panels and legends)
  # te_title(x)      a graph title, wrapped onto a second line when it is longer than 55 characters
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
fit_size <- function(n, at = 10) max(8, min(10, 10 * at / max(n, 1)))
wrap_at  <- function(width) function(x) str_wrap(x, width)
te_title <- function(x) str_wrap(x, 55)

  # [Diagnostic graphs shared by ANOVA and regression] ===============================================================================================
  # qq_band()    The Q-Q points and band, drawn like car::qqPlot(): the line runs through the 1st and 3rd quartiles, and the band is a 95% pointwise
  #              confidence envelope around it. For each point, P = its plotting position, z = the matching normal quantile, and se = the standard
  #              error of that order statistic.
  # qq_check()   The normality check used instead of a test: how many residuals fall outside the band. Even normal residuals put about 5% outside
  #              by chance, so they are only judged "not normal" when more than QQ_OUTSIDE (10%) do. Returns list(n_out, n, share, normal).
  # qq_plot()    The Q-Q plot itself, with the band shaded.
  # resid_plot() Residuals vs. fitted values, with a dashed line at 0. ANOVA fitted values repeat for each group, so jitter spreads the points sideways
  #              (width = 3% of the fitted-value range, with a fallback value if the range is 0); regression uses plain points. Labels and the theme
  #              are added last, then the plot is returned.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
qq_band <- function(res) {
  x  <- sort(res[is.finite(res)]); n <- length(x)
  P  <- stats::ppoints(n); z <- stats::qnorm(P)
  qx <- stats::quantile(x, c(.25, .75), names = FALSE); qz <- stats::qnorm(c(.25, .75))
  b  <- diff(qx) / diff(qz); a <- qx[1] - b * qz[1]           # slope and intercept of the quartile line
  se <- (b / stats::dnorm(z)) * sqrt(P * (1 - P) / n)
  tibble(z = z, x = x, line = a + b * z, lo = line - 1.96 * se, hi = line + 1.96 * se)
}
qq_check <- function(res) {
  d <- qq_band(res)
  n_out <- sum(d$x < d$lo | d$x > d$hi)
  list(n_out = n_out, n = nrow(d), share = n_out / nrow(d), normal = n_out / nrow(d) <= QQ_OUTSIDE)
}
qq_plot <- function(res, title = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals") {
  ggplot(qq_band(res), aes(z)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "#00BCD4", alpha = .18) +
    geom_line(aes(y = lo), colour = "#20B2AA", linetype = "dashed") + geom_line(aes(y = hi), colour = "#20B2AA", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(aes(y = line), colour = "#2E8B57", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = x), colour = "#1B5E4B", alpha = .6) +
    x_axis(n = 6) + y_axis() +
    labs(title = title, x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles (Residuals)",
         caption = "Shaded band = 95% confidence envelope") + te_theme()
}
resid_plot <- function(fitted, res, jitter = FALSE, title = "Residuals vs. Fitted Values") {
  w <- 0.03 * diff(range(fitted)); if (!is.finite(w) || w == 0) w <- 0.01
  p <- ggplot(tibble(f = fitted, r = res), aes(f, r)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#1B5E4B")
  p <- p + if (jitter) geom_jitter(width = w, height = 0, colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = .45)
           else        geom_point(colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = .45)
  p + x_axis(n = 6) + y_axis() + labs(title = title, x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals") + te_theme()
}

  # [safe_levene()] ==================================================================================================================================
  # Levene's test (car::leveneTest, centred on group medians as car does by default): do the groups have equal spread? Returns list(stat, p), with NA
  # values if the test can't run.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
safe_levene <- function(y, g) {
  lt <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(car::leveneTest(y ~ g, data = tibble(y = y, g = factor(g)))), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(lt)) list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_) else list(stat = lt$`F value`[1], p = lt$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}

  # [assumption_tbl() and qq_note()] =================================================================================================================
  # assumption_tbl()  The "Assumption checks" table shared by ANOVA and regression: Levene's test (equal spread) with a plain-English reading.
  #                   lev = a safe_levene() result; lev_name = how the row is labelled.
  # qq_note()         One sentence reporting qq_check() (qc), shown under the table so students can see how normality was judged.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
assumption_tbl <- function(lev, lev_name = "Levene's Test (Equal variances)") {
  tibble(Test = lev_name, Statistic = lev$stat, `p-value` = fmt_p(lev$p), Interpretation = interp(lev$p))
}
qq_note <- function(qc, label = "Normality") {
  tags$p(tags$strong(paste0(label, " (Q-Q plot): ")),
         sprintf("%d of %d residuals (%.1f%%) fall outside the 95%% band. %s", qc$n_out, qc$n, 100 * qc$share,
                 if (qc$normal) sprintf("That is %.0f%% or fewer, so the residuals look approximately normal.", 100 * QQ_OUTSIDE)
                 else sprintf("That is more than %.0f%%, so the residuals do not look normal.", 100 * QQ_OUTSIDE)))
}

  # [interp()] =======================================================================================================================================
  # Plain-English reading of a diagnostic p-value (p at or above ALPHA = no evidence the assumption is broken).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
interp <- function(p) case_when(is.na(p)    ~ "Could not be computed",
                                p >= ALPHA  ~ "No evidence of a violation",
                                .default    = "Possible violation - interpret with caution")

  # [conclusion_ui()] ================================================================================================================================
  # Written conclusion shown under each test: reject_txt is shown when p < ALPHA, fail_txt when it is not. The sentence is chosen by: p missing /
  # reject H0 (p < ALPHA) / fail to reject H0. Subscript zero is written as a Unicode escape.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
conclusion_ui <- function(p, reject_txt, fail_txt) {
  txt <- if (is.na(p)) "The p-value could not be computed."
         else if (p < ALPHA) sprintf("The p-value (%s) is less than %.2f, so we reject H\u2080. %s", fmt_p(p), ALPHA, reject_txt)
         else sprintf("The p-value (%s) is not less than %.2f, so we fail to reject H\u2080. %s", fmt_p(p), ALPHA, fail_txt)
  tags$p(class = "concl", tags$strong(sprintf("Conclusion (\u03b1 = %.2f): ", ALPHA)), txt)
}

  # [D8. DESIGNER SECTION (statistics)] ==============================================================================================================
  # Per the project plan, the statistics code and the test explanations are meant to be written/owned by the project designer. What follows is a
  # working, plain-R starting point: one analysis function per test, plus the explanation text. Replace or rewrite any of it - the rest of the app
  # only needs each function to return the same named list (see ANOVA below).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================

  # [1. ANOVA: quantitative response + qualitative explanatory] ======================================================================================
  # yvar = quantitative response column name; gvar = qualitative grouping column name. Returns a named list (type, title, main_plot, summary_ui,
  # test_ui, diag_plots, diag_ui): the 'contract' the results page expects from every analyse_* function. Two entries are optional: plot_height
  # (a taller main graph, used by chi-squared) and diag_titles (headings over each pair of diagnostic plots, used by regression).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analyse_anova <- function(df, yvar, gvar) {
  n_orig <- n_distinct(df[[gvar]], na.rm = TRUE)               # group count before lumping
  d <- tibble(y = df[[yvar]], g = lump_levels(df[[gvar]]))      # y = the numbers, g = the group
  d <- drop_na(d)                                               # keep rows where both values exist
  d <- filter(d, g %in% names(which(table(g) >= 2)))            # a group needs 2+ values for spread
  d <- mutate(d, g = fct_drop(g))                               # forget group labels with no rows
  validate(need(nlevels(d$g) >= 2 && nrow(d) > nlevels(d$g),    # friendly message if it can't run
                "ANOVA needs at least two groups that each have 2 or more observations."))

  fit  <- stats::aov(y ~ g, data = d)  # fit the ANOVA model: y explained by group
  tab  <- summary(fit)[[1]]            # the ANOVA table as a data frame
  pval <- tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]              # p-value of the F-test
  res  <- stats::resid(fit)            # residuals (each value minus its group mean)
  ylab <- var_label(yvar); glab <- var_label(gvar); ng <- nlevels(d$g)
  # -- Graph --
  # Boxplots + (thinned) raw points. Group names wrap after 14 characters and shrink when there are many groups; with more than 4 groups they are
  # also tilted.
  pts  <- if (nrow(d) > 4000) slice_sample(d, n = 4000) else d
  main_plot <- ggplot(d, aes(g, y, fill = g)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = .55, outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(data = pts, width = .15, alpha = .25, size = .8, colour = "#1B5E4B") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = te_cols(ng)) + guides(fill = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_at(14)) + y_axis() +
    labs(title = te_title(paste(ylab, "by", glab)), x = glab, y = ylab) + te_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = fit_size(ng), angle = if (ng > 4) 40 else 0, hjust = if (ng > 4) 1 else .5, vjust = 1))
  # -- Numerical summary by group --
  # One row per group: n, mean, sd, median, min, max. A note is only shown when groups were lumped into 'Other'.
  by_g <- d %>%
    group_by(Group = g) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(y), sd = stats::sd(y), median = stats::median(y), min = min(y), max = max(y))
  note <- NULL
  if (n_orig > TOP_LEVELS) note <- sprintf("%s has %d different values; only the %d most common are kept and the rest are grouped as \"Other\".", glab, n_orig, TOP_LEVELS)
  # -- ANOVA table + diagnostic tests --
  # Levene's test asks: do the groups have equal spread? qq_check() asks: are the residuals normal (do they stay inside the Q-Q band)?
  anova_tbl <- tibble(Source = c("Between Groups", "Within Groups (Residuals)"),
                      Df = tab$Df, `Sum Sq` = tab$`Sum Sq`, `Mean Sq` = tab$`Mean Sq`,
                      `F value` = c(tab$`F value`[1], NA), `p-value` = c(fmt_p(pval), ""))
  qc       <- qq_check(res)
  diag_tbl <- assumption_tbl(safe_levene(d$y, d$g))
  # -- Tukey HSD contrasts --
  # Every pair of groups compared, with the family-wise error rate held at ALPHA. One row per pair: difference in means, its confidence interval and
  # the adjusted p-value. TukeyHSD names each row "B-A"; pair_lab maps those names to "B − A" (built from the levels, so hyphens inside a group name
  # are left alone).
  tk <- stats::TukeyHSD(fit, conf.level = 1 - ALPHA)$g
  pr <- utils::combn(levels(d$g), 2)
  pair_lab  <- setNames(paste(pr[2, ], "−", pr[1, ]), paste(pr[2, ], pr[1, ], sep = "-"))
  tukey_tbl <- tibble(Comparison = unname(pair_lab[rownames(tk)]), Difference = tk[, "diff"],
                      `CI Lower` = tk[, "lwr"], `CI Upper` = tk[, "upr"], `Adjusted p-value` = fmt_p(tk[, "p adj"]),
                      Significant = if_else(tk[, "p adj"] < ALPHA, "Yes", "No"))
  # -- Kruskal-Wallis --
  # Only added when the Q-Q check finds non-normal residuals: compares the groups using ranks, so it does not need normality.
  kw_ui <- NULL
  if (!qc$normal) {
    kw <- stats::kruskal.test(y ~ g, data = d)
    kw_ui <- tagList(
      tags$h4("Kruskal-Wallis Test (Residuals are not normal)"),
      tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("%.1f%% of the residuals fall outside the Q-Q plot's 95%% band (more than %.0f%%), so they do not look normal. This rank-based test is given as a check on the ANOVA. It asks whether the groups' distributions (roughly, their medians) differ.", 100 * qc$share, 100 * QQ_OUTSIDE)),
      html_table(tibble(Statistic = c("Kruskal-Wallis χ²", "Degrees of freedom", "p-value"),
                        Value = c(fmt_n(kw$statistic), as.character(kw$parameter), fmt_p(kw$p.value))), "Kruskal-Wallis Test"),
      conclusion_ui(kw$p.value, "At least one group tends to have larger or smaller values than the others.",
                    "There is not enough evidence that the groups differ."))
  }

  # -- Contrasts box --
  # The Tukey table can run to 45+ rows, so it sits in a collapsible box (closed at first) whose heading already says how many pairs differ.
  contrasts_ui <- tags$details(class = "contrasts",
    tags$summary(sprintf("Pairwise Contrasts (Tukey HSD, %.0f%% confidence intervals): %d of %d pairs differ significantly",
                         100 * (1 - ALPHA), sum(tk[, "p adj"] < ALPHA), nrow(tk))),
    html_table(tukey_tbl),
    tags$p(class = "note", "Each row compares two group means. A pair differs significantly when its adjusted p-value is below α (its confidence interval does not include 0)."))

  list(type = "anova", title = paste("ANOVA:", ylab, "by", glab),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(by_g, paste("Summary of", ylab, "for Each", glab, "Group")),
                            if (!is.null(note)) tags$p(class = "note", note)),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(anova_tbl, "ANOVA Table"),
                         conclusion_ui(pval, "At least one group mean differs from the others.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence that any group mean differs."),
                         contrasts_ui,
                         kw_ui),
       diag_plots = list(qq_plot(res), resid_plot(stats::fitted(fit), res, jitter = TRUE)),
       diag_ui = tagList(html_table(diag_tbl, "Assumption Checks"), qq_note(qc),
                         tags$p(class = "note", "With very large samples Levene's test flags tiny, unimportant differences in spread - judge the plots too.")))
}

  # [2. Simple linear regression: quantitative + quantitative] =======================================================================================
  # yvar = response column name; xvar = explanatory column name (both quantitative). Returns the same named list as analyse_anova().
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analyse_regression <- function(df, yvar, xvar) {
  d <- tibble(y = df[[yvar]], x = df[[xvar]])      # working table: y = response, x = explanatory
  d <- drop_na(d)
  validate(need(nrow(d) >= 3 && stats::sd(d$x) > 0 && stats::sd(d$y) > 0,  # 3+ rows, both vary
                "Regression needs at least 3 complete observations where both variables vary."))
  yl <- var_label(yvar); xl <- var_label(xvar)   # the two names as shown on the page ("Sample pH")
  # -- fit_slr() --
  # Fits y ~ x for one version of the response (the original, or log(y) below) and returns everything shown for that fit: the model, its summary,
  # residuals, the coefficient table, the overall F-test p-value, the Q-Q normality check, and Levene's test. Levene's test needs groups, so the
  # residuals are split into two groups at the median fitted value (the "modified Levene" test for regression): equal spread means both halves
  # scatter about the same.
  fit_slr <- function(yy, ylab) {
    fit <- stats::lm(yy ~ d$x)        # fit the straight-line model
    s   <- summary(fit)              # summary of the fit: coefficients, R-squared, F-statistic
    cf  <- s$coefficients            # coefficient table (estimate, std. error, t, p)
    ci  <- stats::confint(fit)       # 95% confidence intervals for the coefficients
    res <- stats::resid(fit)         # residuals (observed minus predicted)
    fv  <- stats::fitted(fit)
    qc  <- qq_check(res)
    lev <- safe_levene(res, if_else(fv <= stats::median(fv), "Lower half", "Upper half"))
    fp  <- stats::pf(s$fstatistic[1], s$fstatistic[2], s$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)  # p-value of the overall F-test
    list(s = s, cf = cf, res = res, fv = fv, qc = qc, lev = lev,
         coef_tbl = tibble(Term = c("Intercept (β₀)", paste0("Slope (β₁): ", xl)),
                           Estimate = cf[, 1], `Std. Error` = cf[, 2], `t value` = cf[, 3],
                           `p-value` = fmt_p(cf[, 4]), `95% CI Lower` = ci[, 1], `95% CI Upper` = ci[, 2]),
         diag_tbl = assumption_tbl(lev, "Levene's Test (Equal spread: lower vs. upper half of fitted values)"),
         f_line = tags$p(sprintf("Overall model F-test (Response: %s): F = %s on %d and %d df, p-value %s", ylab,
                                 fmt_n(s$fstatistic[1]), s$fstatistic[2], s$fstatistic[3], fmt_p(fp))))
  }
  m  <- fit_slr(d$y, yl)
  s  <- m$s; cf <- m$cf
  # -- Graph --
  # Scatterplot (fainter when there are many points) with the least-squares line.
  main_plot <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = if (nrow(d) > 500) .3 else .6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "#2E8B57") +
    x_axis() + y_axis() +
    labs(title = te_title(paste(yl, "vs.", xl)), x = xl, y = yl, caption = "Line = least-squares fit") + te_theme()

  desc <- d %>%                                                 # descriptive stats, both variables
    pivot_longer(c(y, x), names_to = "role", values_to = "v") %>%  # one long column of values, labelled y or x
    mutate(Variable = if_else(role == "y", paste0(yl, " (Response)"), paste0(xl, " (Explanatory)")),
           Variable = fct_inorder(Variable)) %>%                   # keep the response first
    group_by(Variable) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(v), sd = stats::sd(v), median = stats::median(v), min = min(v), max = max(v))
  # fit_tbl  strength of the fit: correlation, R-squared, adjusted R-squared, residual standard error
  fit_tbl <- tibble(Statistic = c("Correlation (r)", "R\u00b2", "Adjusted R\u00b2", "Residual standard error"),
                    Value = c(stats::cor(d$x, d$y), s$r.squared, s$adj.r.squared, s$sigma))
  # -- Automatic log(y) refit --
  # If either assumption check on the original fit fails (residuals outside the Q-Q band, or Levene's test), the model is refitted with log(y), which
  # often evens out skewed responses and spread that grows with y. log() needs every y above 0, so a response with zeros or negatives gets a note
  # instead.
  failed  <- !m$qc$normal || isTRUE(m$lev$p < ALPHA)
  log_ui  <- NULL; log_diag <- NULL; log_plots <- list()
  if (failed && min(d$y) <= 0) {
    log_ui <- tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("An assumption check failed, but a log transformation was not tried because %s has values of 0 or below.", yl))
  } else if (failed) {
    lg <- fit_slr(log(d$y), paste0("Log(", yl, ")"))
    b1 <- lg$cf[2, 1]
    log_ui <- tagList(
      tags$h4(sprintf("Log-Transformed Analysis: Log(%s) on %s", yl, xl)),
      tags$p(class = "note", "At least one assumption check failed for the original data, so the model was refitted using the natural log of the response."),
      html_table(lg$coef_tbl, sprintf("Regression Coefficients (Response: log(%s))", yl)),
      lg$f_line,
      tags$p(sprintf("Interpretation: each 1-unit increase in %s multiplies %s by e^%s = %s, a change of about %s%%.",
                     xl, yl, fmt_n(b1, 4), fmt_n(exp(b1), 4), fmt_n(100 * (exp(b1) - 1), 2))),
      conclusion_ui(lg$cf[2, 4], sprintf("There is evidence of a linear relationship between log(%s) and %s.", yl, xl),
                    sprintf("There is not enough evidence of a linear relationship between log(%s) and %s.", yl, xl)))
    log_diag  <- tagList(html_table(lg$diag_tbl, sprintf("Assumption Checks After the Log Transformation (Log(%s))", yl)),
```
