```{r}
                         qq_note(lg$qc, sprintf("Normality after the log transformation (Log(%s))", yl)))
    log_plots <- list(qq_plot(lg$res), resid_plot(lg$fv, lg$res))  # the "Log Transformation" heading above them names the model (diag_titles)
  }

  list(type = "regression", title = paste("Simple Linear Regression:", yl, "on", xl),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       diag_titles = if (length(log_plots)) c(paste("Original Model:", yl), sprintf("Log Transformation: Log(%s)", yl)),  # headings over each pair
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(desc, "Descriptive Statistics"), html_table(fit_tbl, "Strength of the Linear Relationship")),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(m$coef_tbl, "Regression Coefficients"),
                         m$f_line,
                         conclusion_ui(cf[2, 4], "There is evidence of a linear relationship between the two variables.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence of a linear relationship."),
                         log_ui),
       diag_plots = c(list(qq_plot(m$res), resid_plot(m$fv, m$res)), log_plots),  # Q-Q first, then residuals vs. fitted (2 x 2 with the log refit)
       diag_ui = tagList(html_table(m$diag_tbl, "Assumption Checks"), qq_note(m$qc),
                         tags$p(class = "note", "Also check the Residuals vs. Fitted plot: a random cloud around 0 supports linearity and equal spread."),
                         log_diag))
}

  # [3. Chi-squared test of independence: qualitative + qualitative] =================================================================================
  # v1 = ROW variable (the app passes the explanatory variable); v2 = COLUMN variable (the response). Both qualitative. Returns the same named list as
  # analyse_anova(). n1 and n2 count each variable's categories before lumping (used for the note below). In the working table d, a = first variable
  # and b = second (rare categories lumped into 'Other').
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analyse_chisq <- function(df, v1, v2) {
  n1 <- n_distinct(df[[v1]], na.rm = TRUE); n2 <- n_distinct(df[[v2]], na.rm = TRUE)
  d  <- tibble(a = lump_levels(df[[v1]]), b = lump_levels(df[[v2]]))
  n_all <- nrow(d)                                  # every row in the table
  d  <- drop_na(d)                                  # only rows where BOTH variables are filled in
  d  <- mutate(d, a = fct_drop(a), b = fct_drop(b)) # forget category labels with no rows left
  if (nlevels(d$a) < 2 || nlevels(d$b) < 2 || nrow(d) == 0) {
    # -- Explain WHY --
    # A variable can look varied on its own yet be left with one category once the rows where the other variable is blank are removed (e.g. soil_type
    # is only filled in for soil samples).
    left <- function(f, nm) if (nlevels(f) == 1) sprintf("%s has only one category (\"%s\")", nm, levels(f))
                            else sprintf("%s has %d categories", nm, nlevels(f))
    validate(need(FALSE, sprintf(
      "The chi-squared test needs at least two categories in each variable, using only rows where both are filled in. Only %s of %s rows have both %s and %s filled in; among those rows, %s and %s.",
      format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), format(n_all, big.mark = ","), var_label(v1), var_label(v2), left(d$a, var_label(v1)), left(d$b, var_label(v2)))))
  }
  # -- Run the test --
  # Contingency table (the count for every combination of categories), then the test with no continuity correction. Small-count warnings are reported
  # by our own check below.
  tab  <- table(d$a, d$b)
  test <- suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))
  expd <- test$expected   # counts we would expect if the variables were independent
  low  <- sum(expd < 5)   # how many cells have an expected count below 5
  n    <- sum(tab)        # total sample size
  note <- NULL            # a note is only shown when categories were lumped into 'Other'
  if (max(n1, n2) > TOP_LEVELS) note <- sprintf("Variables with more than %d categories keep only their %d most common; the rest are grouped as \"Other\".", TOP_LEVELS, TOP_LEVELS)
  # -- Graph --
  # Column graph of the response (v2): one panel per category of the explanatory variable (v1), one column per response category, named under the
  # column (no legend). A thin border around each panel keeps neighbouring panels apart. Panel names wrap after 18 characters, column names after
  # 12 and shrink when there are many; when more than 8 column names share a row they are also tilted. Up to 4 panels share a row, and the graph
  # grows 190 px taller for each row past the first two. The border's linetype is set because the Economist theme makes outlines invisible.
  l1 <- var_label(v1); l2 <- var_label(v2); na <- nlevels(d$a); nb <- nlevels(d$b)
  ncols <- min(na, if (na <= 4) 2 else 4)
  nrows <- ceiling(na / ncols)
  tilt  <- nb * ncols > 8
  plot_df <- count(d, a, b, .drop = FALSE)          # every a/b combination, including zero counts
  main_plot <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(b, n, fill = b)) +
    geom_col(colour = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~ a, ncol = ncols, labeller = as_labeller(wrap_at(18))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = te_cols(nb)) + guides(fill = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = wrap_at(12)) + y_axis(n = 4, pad = c(0, .08)) +
    labs(title = te_title(paste(l2, "by", l1)), subtitle = paste("Panels:", l1), x = l2, y = "Count") + te_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = fit_size(nb * ncols, at = 8), angle = if (tilt) 35 else 0, hjust = if (tilt) 1 else .5, vjust = 1),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey55", fill = NA, linewidth = .4, linetype = "solid"), panel.spacing = unit(10, "pt"),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1B5E4B", size = fit_size(na)))

  counts_tbl <- as.data.frame.matrix(stats::addmargins(tab)) %>%              # with row/column totals
    rownames_to_column("Level")
  pct_tbl    <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(100 * prop.table(tab, 1), 1)) %>%  # row % (each row = 100)
    rownames_to_column("Level")
  # -- Test results and diagnostics --
  # test_tbl  statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, n
  # mc        optional note with a Monte Carlo (simulation-based) p-value, used when many expected counts are small
  # exp_tbl   expected counts, formatted for display
  # pres_tbl  Pearson residuals, (O - E) / sqrt(E): how strongly each cell departs from independence (beyond about 2 = a lot)
  test_tbl <- tibble(Statistic = c("Chi-squared (\u03c7\u00b2)", "Degrees of freedom", "p-value", "Sample size (n)"),
                     Value = c(fmt_n(test$statistic), as.character(test$parameter), fmt_p(test$p.value), as.character(n)))
  mc <- NULL
  if (low / length(expd) > 0.2) {  # many small expected counts: add a simulation-based p-value
    set.seed(1)
    mcp <- stats::chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000)$p.value
    mc  <- tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("Because %d%% of cells have an expected count below 5, a simulation-based (Monte Carlo) p-value is also given: %s.", round(100 * low / length(expd)), fmt_p(mcp)))
  }
  exp_tbl  <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(expd, 2)) %>% rownames_to_column("Level")
  pres_tbl <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(test$residuals, 2)) %>% rownames_to_column("Level")

  list(type = "chisq", title = paste("Chi-squared Test of Independence:", l1, "and", l2),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       plot_height = if (nrows > 2) 440 + 190 * (nrows - 2) else NULL,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(counts_tbl, sprintf("Counts (Rows: %s; columns: %s)", l1, l2)),
                            html_table(pct_tbl, "Row Percentages (Each row adds to 100%)"),
                            if (!is.null(note)) tags$p(class = "note", note)),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(test_tbl, "Chi-squared Test"), mc,
                         conclusion_ui(test$p.value, "The two variables appear to be associated.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence that the variables are associated.")),
       diag_plots = list(),
       diag_ui = tagList(
         tags$p(sprintf("Cells with expected count below 5: %d of %d (%.0f%%). Smallest expected count: %s.",
                        low, length(expd), 100 * low / length(expd), fmt_n(min(expd), 2))),
         tags$p(class = "note", "Rule of thumb: all expected counts should be at least 1, and at least 80% should be 5 or more."),
         html_table(exp_tbl, "Expected Counts (If the variables were independent)"),
         html_table(pres_tbl, "Pearson Residuals, (O \u2212 E) / \u221aE (Beyond about \u00b12 = cell contributes strongly)")))
}

  # [4. Simple logistic regression: two-outcome qualitative response + quantitative explanatory] ======================================================
  # yvar = response column name (exactly two outcomes, see binary_outcome()); xvar = explanatory column name (quantitative). Returns the same named
  # list as analyse_anova(). In the working table d, out = the outcome as text, x = the explanatory value, y = 1 if out is the event, else 0.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analyse_logistic <- function(df, yvar, xvar) {
  bo <- binary_outcome(df[[yvar]])
  validate(need(!is.null(bo), "Logistic regression needs a response with exactly two outcomes (such as Yes / No)."))
  n_inc <- sum(!is.na(df[[yvar]]) & is.na(bo$y))              # rows dropped as Inconclusive / did not grow
  d <- tibble(out = bo$y, x = df[[xvar]]) %>% drop_na() %>% mutate(y = as.integer(out == bo$event))
  validate(need(nrow(d) >= 10 && n_distinct(d$y) == 2 && stats::sd(d$x) > 0,
                "Logistic regression needs at least 10 complete rows, both outcomes present, and an explanatory variable that varies."))
  ev  <- paste(bo$event); ylab <- var_label(yvar); xlab <- var_label(xvar)

  fit  <- suppressWarnings(stats::glm(y ~ x, family = stats::binomial, data = d))  # warnings (separation) are reported below instead
  cf   <- summary(fit)$coefficients                              # estimate (log-odds), std. error, z, p
  ci   <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(tryCatch(stats::confint(fit), error = function(e) stats::confint.default(fit))))  # 95% CIs (profile; Wald if that fails)
  phat <- stats::fitted(fit)                                     # predicted probability of the event for each row
  # "Perfect separation": x splits the two outcomes (almost) perfectly, so the fit runs off to infinity and the estimates, odds ratios and z-test
  # p-values are meaningless. The plain-English interpretation is replaced by a warning when this happens.
  separate <- !fit$converged || any(phat < 1e-6 | phat > 1 - 1e-6)
  # -- Likelihood-ratio test and fit --
  # The LRT compares this model with one that ignores x: the drop in deviance is chi-squared on 1 df.
  lrt   <- fit$null.deviance - fit$deviance
  lrt_p <- stats::pchisq(lrt, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  b1   <- cf[2, 1]; or <- exp(b1)
  q     <- stats::quantile(d$x, c(.25, .75), names = FALSE)     # predicted probability at the 1st and 3rd quartiles of x
  pq    <- stats::predict(fit, tibble(x = q), type = "response")

  # -- Graph --
  # Each row is a faint point at 1 (event) or 0 (not), jittered up/down a little; the line is the fitted S-shaped probability curve. Half-transparent
  # cyan lines mark Y = 1 and Y = 0 (the two possible outcomes) and a sky-blue dotted line marks Y = 0.5 (a 50/50 chance), to help the eye.
  grid <- tibble(x = seq(min(d$x), max(d$x), length.out = 200))
  grid$p <- stats::predict(fit, grid, type = "response")
  main_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, 1), colour = "#00ACC1", linewidth = 1, alpha = .5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .5, colour = "#4FC3F7", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = .9) +
    geom_jitter(data = d, aes(x, y), width = 0, height = .03, colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = if (nrow(d) > 500) .2 else .4) +
    geom_line(data = grid, aes(x, p), colour = "#2E8B57", linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, .25), limits = c(-.05, 1.05)) + x_axis() +
    labs(title = te_title(paste0("Probability of ", ylab, " = ", ev, " by ", xlab)), x = xlab,
         y = str_wrap(paste0("Probability ", ylab, " = ", ev), 30),
         caption = paste0("Points: 1 = ", ev, ", 0 = ", bo$other, ". Line = fitted logistic curve.")) +
    te_theme()

  # -- Numerical summary --
  # The explanatory variable described separately for each outcome, plus a note on any Inconclusive rows left out.
  by_out <- d %>% group_by(Outcome = out) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), median = stats::median(x), min = min(x), max = max(x))
  inc_note <- if (n_inc > 0) tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("%d row(s) recorded as Inconclusive or Isolate did not grow are left out, because they are not one of the two outcomes.", n_inc))

  # -- Coefficient and fit tables --
  # coef_tbl  log-odds estimates with their odds ratios (e^estimate) and 95% CIs. For the intercept the "odds ratio" is the odds of the event when
  #           x = 0.
  # fit_tbl   deviances and the likelihood-ratio test
  coef_tbl <- tibble(Term = c("Intercept (\u03b2\u2080)", paste0("Slope (\u03b2\u2081): ", xlab)),
                     `Estimate (Log-odds)` = cf[, 1], `Std. Error` = cf[, 2], `z value` = cf[, 3], `p-value` = fmt_p(cf[, 4]),
                     `Odds Ratio` = exp(cf[, 1]), `OR 95% CI Lower` = exp(ci[, 1]), `OR 95% CI Upper` = exp(ci[, 2]))
  fit_tbl <- tibble(Statistic = c("Null deviance (No x)", "Residual deviance (With x)", "Likelihood-ratio \u03c7\u00b2 (1 df)", "p-value", "Sample size (n)"),
                    Value = c(fmt_n(fit$null.deviance), fmt_n(fit$deviance), fmt_n(lrt), fmt_p(lrt_p), as.character(nrow(d))))
  sep_ui <- tags$p(class = "concl", sprintf("Warning: %s separates the two outcomes almost perfectly (every row on one side of a cut-off has the same outcome), so the estimates and odds ratios above run off toward 0 or infinity and should not be interpreted. The likelihood-ratio test still shows that the two are strongly related.", xlab))
  interp_ui <- if (separate) sep_ui else tags$p(tags$strong("Interpretation: "), sprintf(
    "Each 1-unit increase in %s multiplies the odds that %s = %s by %s (a %s%% %s in the odds). The predicted probability of %s is %.1f%% when %s = %s (1st quartile) and %.1f%% when %s = %s (3rd quartile).",
    xlab, ylab, ev, fmt_n(or, 3), fmt_n(abs(100 * (or - 1)), 1), if (or >= 1) "increase" else "decrease",
    ev, 100 * pq[1], xlab, fmt_n(q[1], 2), 100 * pq[2], xlab, fmt_n(q[2], 2)))

  # -- Diagnostics --
  # hl        Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test: rows are grouped into (up to) 10 bins by predicted probability, and observed event counts are
  #           compared with predicted ones. A small p-value means the S-curve does not fit the data well. Needs 3+ bins (df = bins - 2).
  # small     size of the smaller outcome group; with fewer than 10 the estimates are unreliable.
  g  <- min(10, n_distinct(phat))
  hb <- tibble(p = phat, y = d$y) %>% mutate(bin = ntile(p, g)) %>% group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), obs = sum(y), expd = sum(p))
  hl   <- sum((hb$obs - hb$expd)^2 / (hb$expd * (1 - hb$expd / hb$n)))
  hl_p <- if (g >= 3) stats::pchisq(hl, df = g - 2, lower.tail = FALSE) else NA
  diag_tbl <- tibble(Test = sprintf("Hosmer-Lemeshow (Model fits the data; %d bins)", g),
                     Statistic = if (g >= 3) hl else NA, `p-value` = fmt_p(hl_p), Interpretation = interp(hl_p))
  small    <- min(table(d$y))

  list(type = "logistic", title = paste("Simple Logistic Regression:", ylab, "on", xlab),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(by_out, paste("Summary of", xlab, "for Each", ylab, "Outcome")),
                            tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("The model gives the probability that %s = %s (the other outcome is %s).", ylab, ev, bo$other)),
                            inc_note),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(coef_tbl, "Logistic Regression Coefficients"),
                         html_table(fit_tbl, "Likelihood-Ratio Test and Model Fit"),
                         interp_ui,
                         conclusion_ui(lrt_p, sprintf("%s is associated with the probability that %s = %s.", xlab, ylab, ev),
                                       sprintf("There is not enough evidence that %s is associated with the probability that %s = %s.", xlab, ylab, ev))),
       diag_plots = list(),
       diag_ui = tagList(html_table(diag_tbl, "Assumption Checks"),
                         tags$p(tags$strong("Enough of each outcome: "), sprintf("the smaller outcome has %d rows. %s", small,
                                if (small >= 10) "That is at least 10, which is enough for one explanatory variable."
                                else "That is fewer than 10, so the estimates may be unreliable - interpret with caution.")),
                         if (separate) sep_ui))
}

  # [Explanations (shown under "View More on Test" and in "Learn More")] =============================================================================
  # test_info: the text for each test (name, when it is used, purpose, equations, hypotheses, assumptions). Edit it here to change what 'View More on
  # Test' and 'Learn More' show. Each `model` entry is c(equation, explanation): the equation is shown in a green box and the explanation of its
  # symbols in a pale blue box under it. Math is written in LaTeX between \( and \) and drawn by KaTeX in the browser (see [C2]); in R strings every
  # LaTeX backslash is doubled, e.g. "\\(\\beta_1\\)". \displaystyle makes fractions full size.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
test_info <- list(
  anova = list(
    name = "Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)",
    when = "One quantitative (number) response variable and one qualitative (category) explanatory variable.",
    purpose = "ANOVA asks whether the average of a number variable is different in at least one of the groups. It compares how far apart the group averages are (variation between groups) with how much the values bounce around inside each group (variation within groups). If the group averages are far apart compared with the spread inside the groups, the difference is probably not just chance.",
    model = list(
      c("\\(\\displaystyle Y_{ik} = \\mu + \\alpha_i + \\varepsilon_{ik}, \\qquad \\varepsilon_{ik} \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)\\)",
        "\\(Y_{ik}\\) = the k-th measurement in group i;  \\(\\mu\\) = the overall (grand) average;  \\(\\alpha_i\\) = how far group i's average is from the overall average;  \\(\\varepsilon_{ik}\\) = random error, how far this measurement is from its group's average (assumed normal, centered at 0, with the same spread \\(\\sigma\\) in every group)"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle F = \\frac{\\text{MS Between Groups}}{\\text{MS Within Groups}}\\)",
        "MS = mean square, a measure of variation.  MS Between Groups = how far apart the group averages are;  MS Within Groups = how spread out the values are inside each group.  If \\(H_0\\) is true, F is close to 1; a large F gives a small p-value")),
    hypotheses = c("\\(H_0: \\alpha_i = 0\\) for every group i  (all group averages are equal)",
                   "\\(H_a: \\alpha_i \\neq 0\\) for at least one group i  (at least one group average is different)"),
    assumptions = "Each measurement is independent of the others. The residuals are roughly normal: on the Q-Q plot, no more than 10% of the points fall outside the shaded 95% band. Every group has about the same spread: the residuals vs. fitted plot shows a similar vertical spread for each group, and Levene's test has a p-value above 0.05. ANOVA can handle small departures from these. If the residuals are not normal, the app also runs the Kruskal-Wallis test, which compares ranks instead of averages and does not need normal data. Tukey HSD contrasts then compare every pair of groups to show which ones differ."),
  regression = list(
    name = "Simple Linear Regression",
    when = "Both variables are quantitative (numbers).",
    purpose = "Simple linear regression draws the straight line that best fits a scatterplot. The slope tells how much the response changes, on average, for each 1-unit increase in the explanatory variable. The test asks whether the slope is really different from 0, or whether a flat line (no relationship) could explain the data just as well.",
    model = list(
      c("\\(\\displaystyle Y_i = \\beta_0 + \\beta_1 X_i + \\varepsilon_i, \\qquad \\varepsilon_i \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)\\)",
        "\\(Y_i\\) = the response for row i;  \\(X_i\\) = the explanatory value for row i;  \\(\\beta_0\\) = the true intercept (average Y when X = 0);  \\(\\beta_1\\) = the true slope (change in average Y for each 1-unit increase in X);  \\(\\varepsilon_i\\) = random error, how far the point sits above or below the line"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle \\hat{Y}_i = b_0 + b_1 X_i\\)",
        "The line fitted from the data:  \\(b_0\\) and \\(b_1\\) are our estimates of \\(\\beta_0\\) and \\(\\beta_1\\);  \\(\\hat{Y}_i\\) = the predicted average Y at \\(X_i\\)"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle t = \\frac{b_1}{SE(b_1)}\\)",
        "How many standard errors the estimated slope is away from 0;  \\(R^2\\) = the share of the variation in Y explained by X (from 0 to 1)")),
    hypotheses = c("\\(H_0: \\beta_1 = 0\\)  (no linear relationship; the line is flat)",
                   "\\(H_a: \\beta_1 \\neq 0\\)  (a linear relationship exists)"),
    assumptions = "The relationship follows a straight line. Each point is independent of the others. The residuals are roughly normal: no more than 10% of the points fall outside the Q-Q plot's shaded 95% band. The residuals have the same spread all along the line: no funnel (megaphone) or curved pattern in the residuals vs. fitted plot, and Levene's test comparing the lower and upper halves of the fitted values has a p-value above 0.05. If a check fails and every response value is above 0, the app also fits the model to log(Y), which often straightens a curve and evens out the spread."),
  chisq = list(
    name = "Chi-squared Test of Independence",
    when = "Both variables are qualitative (categories).",
    purpose = "The chi-squared test asks whether two category variables are related. It counts how many rows fall in each combination of categories (observed counts) and compares them with the counts we would expect if the two variables had nothing to do with each other (expected counts). Big gaps between observed and expected counts are evidence that the variables are associated.",
    model = list(
      c("\\(\\displaystyle E_{ij} = \\frac{(\\text{row } i \\text{ total}) \\times (\\text{column } j \\text{ total})}{n}\\)",
        "\\(E_{ij}\\) = the expected count in row i, column j if the variables were independent;  n = the total number of observations"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle \\chi^2 = \\sum \\frac{(O_{ij} - E_{ij})^2}{E_{ij}}, \\qquad df = (r - 1)(c - 1)\\)",
        "O = observed count;  E = expected count;  \\(\\sum\\) = add up over every cell;  r and c = the number of rows and columns;  df = degrees of freedom.  The bigger \\(\\chi^2\\) is, the further the counts are from independence"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle \\text{Pearson residual} = \\frac{O_{ij} - E_{ij}}{\\sqrt{E_{ij}}}\\)",
        "Shows which cells drive the result: positive = more than expected, negative = fewer than expected;  beyond about \\(\\pm 2\\) is a large difference")),
    hypotheses = c("\\(H_0\\): the two variables are independent  (not associated)",
                   "\\(H_a\\): the two variables are associated  (not independent)"),
    assumptions = "Each observation is independent and falls into exactly one cell. The expected counts are large enough for the p-value to be trusted: all are at least 1, and at least 80% are 5 or more. When too many expected counts are small, the app also gives a simulation-based (Monte Carlo) p-value."),
  logistic = list(
    name = "Simple Logistic Regression",
    when = "A qualitative response with exactly two outcomes (such as Yes / No) and a quantitative explanatory variable.",
    purpose = "Logistic regression asks whether the chance of one outcome (for example, antibiotic activity = Yes) goes up or down as the explanatory variable increases. A chance has to stay between 0 and 1, so instead of a straight line it fits an S-shaped curve. The test asks whether the curve really slopes, or whether a flat line (the same chance everywhere) could explain the data just as well.",
    model = list(
      c("\\(\\displaystyle P(Y_i = 1 \\mid x_i) = \\frac{e^{\\beta_0 + \\beta_1 x_i}}{1 + e^{\\beta_0 + \\beta_1 x_i}}\\)",
        "\\(P(Y_i = 1 \\mid x_i)\\) = the chance that row i has the outcome (Y = 1, such as Yes) given its x value;  \\(e \\approx 2.718\\) (a math constant);  \\(\\beta_0\\) = intercept;  \\(\\beta_1\\) = slope (positive: the chance rises as x increases; negative: it falls)"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle \\text{Odds ratio} = e^{\\beta_1}\\)",
        "Odds = \\(\\frac{P}{1 - P}\\), the chance of the outcome divided by the chance of not having it.  The odds ratio is how many times the odds are multiplied for each 1-unit increase in x (1 = no change; above 1 = higher odds; below 1 = lower odds)"),
      c("\\(\\displaystyle \\chi^2_{LR} = \\text{null deviance} - \\text{residual deviance}, \\qquad df = 1\\)",
        "Deviance measures how badly a model misses the data.  Null deviance = misfit of a flat model that ignores x;  residual deviance = misfit with x included.  A big drop means x helps predict the outcome")),
    hypotheses = c("\\(H_0: \\beta_1 = 0\\)  (x does not change the chance of the outcome; odds ratio = 1)",
                   "\\(H_a: \\beta_1 \\neq 0\\)  (x changes the chance of the outcome; odds ratio \\(\\neq\\) 1)"),
    assumptions = "Each row is independent of the others. The S-shaped curve fits the data: the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test has a p-value above 0.05 (here a large p-value is good, because the null hypothesis says the model fits). Each outcome has at least 10 rows, and x does not split the two outcomes perfectly. Rows recorded as Inconclusive are left out.")
)

  # [info_ui()] ======================================================================================================================================
  # Builds the explanation block for one test: when it is used, purpose, mathematical model, hypotheses, and assumptions (diagnostics).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
info_ui <- function(type) {
  i <- test_info[[type]]  # pick the entry for this test
  tagList(
    tags$p(tags$strong("When it is used: "), i$when),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Purpose: "), i$purpose),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Mathematical model:")),
    lapply(i$model, function(m) tagList(tags$div(class = "formula", m[1]), tags$div(class = "formula-note", m[2]))),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Hypotheses:"), style = "margin-top:10px;"), lapply(i$hypotheses, function(m) tags$div(class = "formula", m)),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Assumptions (Diagnostics): "), i$assumptions, style = "margin-top:10px;"))
}

  # [END DESIGNER SECTION] ===========================================================================================================================
  # Everything from [D8] down to here is the designer section.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================

  # [D9. Helpers that build pieces of the page] ======================================================================================================
  # selector_item(): one clickable table name in the Table Selector. Clicking sends the table's name to the server as input$pick_table. The selected
  # row is highlighted.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
selector_item <- function(key, active) {
  tags$a(href = "#", class = paste("te-item", if (active) "active"),
         onclick = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('pick_table', '%s', {priority: 'event'}); return false;", key),
         pretty_name(key))
}

  # [selector_details() and selector_section()] ======================================================================================================
  # A collapsible section of the selector (click the heading to open / close it). `id` names the section so the server can remember whether it was
  # left open, `open` is that remembered state, and `...` is the content inside the section.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
selector_details <- function(id, title, open, ...) {
  tags$details(class = "sel-details", open = if (open) NA,
               ontoggle = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('sec_%s', this.open);", id),
               tags$summary(class = "sel-head", title), ...)
}
selector_section <- function(id, title, keys, current, open = TRUE) {
  selector_details(id, title, open,
                   if (length(keys)) lapply(keys, function(k) selector_item(k, k == current))
                   else tags$p(class = "hint", "No tables found."))
}

  # [pick_row()] =====================================================================================================================================
  # One row of the variable picker: the variable name, then a checkbox in the Response column and a checkbox in the Explanatory column. Ticking calls
  # tePick() (JavaScript above). In box(), data-v holds the variable name for tePick(), and 'checked' restores an earlier tick.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
pick_row <- function(v, type, is_resp, is_expl) {
  box <- function(col, on) tags$input(type = "checkbox", class = paste0("pick-", col), `data-v` = v,
                                      checked = if (on) NA, onclick = sprintf("tePick('%s', this);", col))
  div(class = "pick-row",
      span(class = "pick-name", v, span(class = "vtype", paste0("(", type, ")"))),
      box("resp", is_resp), box("expl", is_expl))
}

  # [plot_box()] =====================================================================================================================================
  # A graph with a download icon in its top-right corner. Clicking the icon opens two links, PDF and PNG, that download the graph through the handlers
  # named <id>_pdf and <id>_png (see "Graph downloads" in [F8]). Choosing a link closes the menu again.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
plot_box <- function(id, width, height) {
  close_menu <- "this.parentNode.open = false;"
  div(class = "dl-box",
      plotOutput(id, width = width, height = height),
      tags$details(class = "dl-menu no-print",
                   tags$summary(title = "Download this graph", icon("download")),
                   downloadLink(paste0(id, "_pdf"), "PDF", onclick = close_menu),
                   downloadLink(paste0(id, "_png"), "PNG", onclick = close_menu)))
}

  # [Graph sizes and diag_groups()] ==================================================================================================================
  # PLOT_RES, PLOT_W, DIAG_W, DIAG_H  graph sizes in pixels; PLOT_RES also turns pixels into inches for the downloads [F8].
  # plot_height()  440 px unless the test asks for more (r$plot_height, e.g. many chi-squared panels).
  # diag_groups()  lays out the diagnostic plots two to a row. When a test names its groups (r$diag_titles, e.g. regression with a log refit), each
  #                pair of plots gets its title above it.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
PLOT_RES <- 110                    # pixels per inch for plots on the page
PLOT_W   <- 780                    # main graph width (px)
DIAG_W   <- 520; DIAG_H <- 360     # diagnostic plot size (px)
plot_height <- function(r) if (is.null(r$plot_height)) 440 else r$plot_height

diag_groups <- function(r) {
  box  <- function(i) plot_box(paste0("diag_plot_", i), width = paste0(DIAG_W, "px"), height = paste0(DIAG_H, "px"))
  n    <- length(r$diag_plots)
  if (is.null(r$diag_titles)) return(div(class = "diag-row", lapply(seq_len(n), box)))
  lapply(seq_along(r$diag_titles), function(g) tagList(
    tags$div(class = "diag-title", r$diag_titles[g]),
    div(class = "diag-row", lapply(intersect(c(2 * g - 1, 2 * g), seq_len(n)), box))))
}
```

```{r}
# [E. PAGE SHELL (rendered once)] ====================================================================================================================
# Everything inside "page" is filled in by the server section below.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
# BANNER_ART: a close-up of soil bacteria (rods with flagella and a coccus cluster) drawn in pale cyan for the right end of the banner. The drawing is
# larger than the banner on purpose, so the cells are cut off at its edges; the fade and position are set in CSS [B2] (.te-banner-art).
BANNER_ART <- '
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 80" preserveAspectRatio="xMaxYMid slice" aria-hidden="true">
  <g fill="#B2EBF2" fill-opacity=".7" stroke="#E0F7FA" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round">
    <rect x="165" y="-10" width="175" height="58" rx="29" transform="rotate(-16 252 19)"/>
    <rect x="198" y="50" width="120" height="40" rx="20" transform="rotate(12 258 70)"/>
    <rect x="62" y="4" width="66" height="26" rx="13" transform="rotate(24 95 17)"/>
    <circle cx="140" cy="44" r="13"/><circle cx="160" cy="62" r="11"/><circle cx="128" cy="68" r="9"/>
  </g>
  <g fill="none" stroke="#00ACC1" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round">
    <path d="M200 30 q10 -10 20 0 t20 0 t20 0 t20 -2"/>
    <path d="M222 72 q8 -7 16 0 t16 0 t16 2"/>
  </g>
  <g fill="none" stroke="#E0F7FA" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-opacity=".9">
    <path d="M170 48 q-9 9 -18 2 t-18 4 t-16 -4"/>
    <path d="M200 76 q-8 -9 -16 -2 t-16 0 t-14 6"/>
    <path d="M66 26 q-8 6 -15 0 t-14 2"/>
  </g>
</svg>'
tagList(
  div(class = "te-banner",
      div(class = "te-banner-art", HTML(BANNER_ART)),
      h1("Tiny Earth Public Database \u2013 BIO 181 Lab Analysis App"),
      p("Explore soil-bacteria data from the Tiny Earth Public Database and test relationships between variables using statistics",
        "\u00b7 University of Wisconsin\u2013Madison \u00b7 BYU-Idaho")),
  uiOutput("page"))  # placeholder: see output$page in the server section [F2]
```

```{r}
#| context: server
# [F. SERVER] ========================================================================================================================================
# Runs separately for EACH visitor, so one student's clicks never affect another student's session.
# ====================================================================================================================================================

  # [F1. This visitor's app state] ===================================================================================================================
  #   page     : "viewer" (data viewer) or "results" (analysis page)
  #   mode     : "browse" (table selector) or "select" (pick two variables)
  #   view     : "table" (Table Viewer) or "description" (Variable Description)
  #   table    : the table currently selected
  #   resp     : the variable ticked in the Response column ("" = none yet)
  #   expl     : the variable ticked in the Explanatory column ("" = none yet)
  #   analysis : the table + response + explanatory variable sent to the results page
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
rv <- reactiveValues(page = "viewer", mode = "browse", view = "table",
                     table = if ("samples" %in% all_keys) "samples" else all_keys[1],  # the app opens on Samples
                     resp = "", expl = "", analysis = NULL)

  # [current_df() and table_label()] =================================================================================================================
  # current_df()   the data frame of the selected table. A reactive re-runs by itself whenever rv$table changes.
  # table_label()  text such as 'Samples (Individual)' used in headings.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
current_df   <- reactive({ req(rv$table); load_table(rv$table) })
table_label  <- reactive({ req(rv$table); paste0(pretty_name(rv$table), if (str_detect(rv$table, "_combined$")) " (Combined)" else " (Individual)") })

  # [F2. Which page is showing] ======================================================================================================================
  # No .rds files found: show instructions instead of the app. Viewer: selector / picker card on the left (left_ui), table card on the right
  # (right_ui). Otherwise show the analysis page.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$page <- renderUI({
  if (length(all_keys) == 0)
    return(div(class = "panel-card", h4("No data found"),
               p("The Data folder has no .rds files yet. Run the Data_Clean script first, then restart the app.")))
  if (rv$page == "viewer")
    div(class = "app-grid",
        div(class = "left-col", uiOutput("left_ui")),
        div(uiOutput("right_ui")))
  else
    uiOutput("results_ui")
})

  # [F3. LEFT PANEL: table selector OR variable picker] ==============================================================================================
  # browse = Table Selector; select = variable picker (the else branch below).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$left_ui <- renderUI({
  # Reading rv$page makes the panel rebuild on "Back to Data", so the variable picker shows the ticks that rv$resp / rv$expl still hold (otherwise
  # the boxes come back empty while Analyze still glows).
  req(rv$page == "viewer")
  if (rv$mode == "browse") {
    # -- Table Selector --
    # Each table section is collapsible and starts folded up. Whether it is open is remembered in input$sec_<id> (isolate() = read it now without
    # re-drawing the panel each time one is toggled). The bottom row holds Description (left) and Run Analysis (right). Description shows the Variable
    # Description for the selected table; while that view is open the button is filled in (solid green), reads "Table" (click it to go back), and
    # Run Analysis is greyed out.
    is_open  <- function(id) isTRUE(isolate(input[[paste0("sec_", id)]]))
    in_desc  <- rv$view == "description"
    div(class = "panel-card left-card",
        actionButton("btn_background", "Background", class = "btn-te btn-wide"),
        if (DEBUG_MODE) actionButton("btn_debug", NULL, icon = icon("bug"), class = "btn-te btn-outline btn-square debug-corner has-tip tip-start",
                                     `data-tip` = "Debug: For app development, not intended for student use.",
                                     `aria-label` = "Debug: open each test"),  # opens the Debug window [F12]; pinned to the screen's bottom-left corner
        div(class = "selector-scroll",
            div(class = "sel-title", style = "margin-top:10px;", "Table Selector"),
            selector_section("Individual", "Individual", individual_keys, rv$table, is_open("Individual")),
            selector_section("Combined",   "Combined",   combined_keys,   rv$table, is_open("Combined"))),
        div(class = "btn-row",
            actionButton("btn_desc", if (in_desc) "Table" else "Description",
                         title = if (in_desc) "Back to the Table Viewer" else "Describe every variable in the selected table",
                         class = paste("btn-te", if (!in_desc) "btn-outline")),
            actionButton("btn_run", "Run Analysis", class = "btn-te btn-cyan", disabled = in_desc)))
  } else {
    # -- Variable picker (same card layout as the selector) --
    # Two checkbox columns sit beside every variable: Response (y) and Explanatory (x). isolate() restores earlier ticks without re-drawing the panel
    # on every click.
    df   <- current_df()
    vars <- analysis_vars(df)  # columns worth analysing (see analysis_vars())
    div(class = "panel-card left-card",
        div(class = "sel-title", "Select two variables."),
        p(class = "hint", "Tick one Response (y) and one Explanatory (x) variable."),
        div(class = "selector-scroll",
            div(class = "pick-head", span("Variable"), span(class = "h-resp", "Response (y)"), span(class = "h-expl", "Explanatory (x)")),
            lapply(vars, function(v) pick_row(v, var_type(df[[v]]), v == isolate(rv$resp), v == isolate(rv$expl)))),
        uiOutput("sel_status"),
        div(class = "btn-row",
            actionButton("btn_back", "Back", class = "btn-te btn-outline"),
            uiOutput("analyse_btn", inline = TRUE)))
  }
})

  # [F4. Variable picker status and Analyze button] ==================================================================================================
  # pair_test()          which test fits the ticked pair? NA until both columns have a variable (or if no test fits).
  # output$sel_status    message under the variable list: progress, a warning for a pair with no test, or the test that will run. n = how many columns
  #                      have a tick (0, 1 or 2).
  # output$analyse_btn   "Analyze" is greyed out until a valid Response + Explanatory pair is ticked, then lights up and gently pulses.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
pair_test <- reactive({
  df <- current_df()
  if (!nzchar(rv$resp) || !nzchar(rv$expl)) return(NA_character_)
  pick_test(df[[rv$resp]], df[[rv$expl]])
})

output$sel_status <- renderUI({
  n <- (nzchar(rv$resp)) + (nzchar(rv$expl))
  if (n < 2)                p(class = "hint", sprintf("%d of 2 selected", n))
  else if (is.na(pair_test())) p(class = "concl", "Logistic regression needs a response with exactly two outcomes (such as Yes / No), not counting Inconclusive. Choose a different response, or swap the columns.")
  else                      p(class = "hint", "Ready: ", tags$strong(test_info[[pair_test()]]$name))
})

output$analyse_btn <- renderUI({
  if (!is.na(pair_test())) actionButton("btn_analyse", "Analyze", class = "btn-te btn-glow")
  else actionButton("btn_analyse", "Analyze", class = "btn-te", disabled = TRUE)
})

  # [F5. RIGHT PANEL: Table Viewer OR Variable Description] ==========================================================================================
  # Table Viewer (the data) or Variable Description (what each column means).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$right_ui <- renderUI({
  if (rv$view == "table") {
    div(class = "panel-card",
        div(class = "viewer-head", h3("Table Viewer"),
            span(class = "current", "Currently Viewing: ", tags$strong(table_label()))),
        DTOutput("data_table"),  # placeholder for the interactive table in output$data_table below
        div(class = "table-foot", textOutput("table_count")))
  } else {
    div(class = "panel-card",
        div(class = "viewer-head", h3("Variable Description"),
            span(class = "current", "Table: ", tags$strong(table_label()))),
        DTOutput("dict_table"),
        div(class = "table-foot", "Each row describes one column (factor) of the selected table."))
  }
})

  # [output$data_table] ==============================================================================================================================
  # The data table: filter boxes sit directly above each column, a search box above the table, scroll bars both ways, and "Showing x to y of N
  # entries" at the bottom. Long text (e.g. DNA sequences) is shortened in the cell; hover to see all of it. trim_js is JavaScript that DataTables
  # runs on each text cell: it cuts text longer than 60 characters and shows the full text as a hover tooltip (esc() makes odd characters safe to
  # show), and defs applies it to the text columns only (nothing if there are none). In datatable(), filter = 'top' puts a filter box above each
  # column; scrollX/scrollY add scroll bars; dom 'lfrtip' = length menu, search box, table, 'Showing x to y of N' line, page buttons.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$data_table <- renderDT({
  df <- current_df()
  text_cols <- unname(which(map_lgl(df, is.character))) - 1
  trim_js <- JS(r"(function(data, type, row) {
      // Only change what is DRAWN; sorting and searching still use the full text.
      if (type === 'display' && data != null && data.length > 60) {
        // esc(): replace characters that have special meaning in HTML.
        var esc = function(s) { return s.replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;'); };
        // Shortened text; the title attribute is the hover tooltip.
        return '<span title="' + esc(data) + '">' + esc(data.substr(0, 60)) + '&hellip;</span>';
      }
      // Anything short (or not being displayed) is returned unchanged.
      return data; }
  )")
  defs <- if (length(text_cols)) list(list(targets = text_cols, render = trim_js)) else list()
  datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", selection = "none", class = "stripe hover compact",
            options = list(scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "52vh", scrollCollapse = TRUE,
                           pageLength = 25, lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50, 100),
                           dom = "lfrtip", columnDefs = defs))
})
output$table_count <- renderText({  # text under the table: rows (data points) and columns (factors)
  df <- current_df()
  sprintf("%s data points (rows) \u00d7 %d factors (columns) in this table.", format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","), ncol(df))
})

  # [output$dict_table: the Variable Description] ======================================================================================================
  # One row per column of the table: name, type, plain-English description, % missing, distinct values, and the first 3 example values. Shown as a
  # table; dom 'ftip' = search box, table, info line, page buttons.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$dict_table <- renderDT({
  df <- current_df(); key <- rv$table
  info <- tibble(
    Variable = names(df),
    Type = map_chr(names(df), ~ describe_type(.x, df[[.x]])),
    Description = map_chr(names(df), ~ lookup_description(key, .x)),
    `% Missing` = map_dbl(df, ~ round(100 * mean(is.na(.x)), 1)),
    `Distinct Values` = map_dbl(df, ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Example Values` = map_chr(df, ~ .x %>% na.omit() %>% as.character() %>% unique() %>% head(3) %>% str_c(collapse = "; ") %>% str_sub(1, 70)))
  datatable(info, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none", class = "stripe hover compact",
            options = list(scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "52vh", scrollCollapse = TRUE, pageLength = 50, dom = "ftip"))
})

  # [F6. Clicks in the viewer] =======================================================================================================================
  # Each observeEvent() runs when its button or input changes. The JavaScript tePick() reports which variable is ticked in each column
  # (input$sel_pair). btn_run opens the variable picker (fresh); btn_back goes back to the table selector.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$pick_table, {                      # chose a different table
  req(input$pick_table %in% all_keys)
  rv$table <- input$pick_table
})
observeEvent(input$btn_desc, {                        # Description / Table: flip between the two views
  rv$view <- if (rv$view == "description") "table" else "description"
})
observeEvent(input$btn_run,  { req(rv$view == "table"); rv$mode <- "select"; rv$resp <- ""; rv$expl <- "" })
observeEvent(input$btn_back, { rv$mode <- "browse"; rv$resp <- ""; rv$expl <- "" })

observeEvent(input$sel_pair, {                       # tePick() reports the ticked pair
  req(rv$page == "viewer", rv$mode == "select")
  rv$resp <- input$sel_pair$resp
  rv$expl <- input$sel_pair$expl
})

observeEvent(input$btn_analyse, {                     # go to the results page
  req(!is.na(pair_test()))
  rv$analysis <- list(table = rv$table, resp = rv$resp, expl = rv$expl)
  rv$page <- "results"
})
observeEvent(input$btn_results_back, { rv$page <- "viewer" })

  # [F7. Background window] ==========================================================================================================================
  # showModal() opens a pop-up window; easyClose lets people click outside it to close. The text inside is ordinary HTML tags and can be edited
  # freely.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$btn_background, {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = "Background", size = "l", easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Close"),
    h4("What is Tiny Earth?"),
    p("Tiny Earth is a student-sourced antibiotic discovery network led by the University of Wisconsin\u2013Madison. Students at schools around the world collect soil samples, isolate bacteria from them, and test those bacteria for antibiotic activity. The results from many schools are shared in the ",
      tags$a(href = "https://publicdata.tinyearth.wisc.edu/", target = "_blank", "Tiny Earth Public Database"), "."),
    h4("What is this app for?"),
    p("This app helps Bio 181 Lab students at BYU\u2013Idaho explore that public data and get a first taste of biostatistics, bioinformatics, and biological data science. You can browse and filter every table, then pick any two variables and the app chooses the right test for you:"),
    tags$ul(
      tags$li(tags$strong("Quantitative response + qualitative explanatory"), " \u2192 Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)"),
      tags$li(tags$strong("Quantitative + quantitative"), " \u2192 Simple Linear Regression"),
      tags$li(tags$strong("Qualitative + qualitative"), " \u2192 Chi-squared Test of Independence"),
      tags$li(tags$strong("Two-outcome qualitative response (e.g. Yes / No) + quantitative explanatory"), " \u2192 Simple Logistic Regression")),
    h4("How to use it"),
    tags$ol(
      tags$li("Pick a table in the Table Selector. Individual tables match the Tiny Earth database; Combined tables add the related sample and institution columns."),
      tags$li("Use the filter boxes above the Table Viewer to search and narrow the data. Use the Description button to see what each column means."),
      tags$li("Press Run Analysis, tick exactly two variables, then press Analyze."),
      tags$li("Read the graphical and numerical summaries, then open View More on Test for the test, its equations, and the assumption checks. Every test uses a 0.05 significance level. Learn More gives a broad guide to the statistics; Save PDF prints the page."),
      tags$li("The round buttons at the top right: the microscope downloads an analysis worksheet (when your instructor has added one), the table lets you explore and download the data you analyzed, and the speech bubble sends feedback.")),
    p(class = "note", "All results are intended for academic and learning purposes.")))
})

  # [F8. RESULTS PAGE] ===============================================================================================================================
  # analysis_type()  "anova", "regression", "chisq" or "logistic", decided by the TYPES of the Response and Explanatory variables chosen in the
  #                  picker. req() waits until an analysis has been requested.
  # result()         runs the matching test function (from the designer section above).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
analysis_type <- reactive({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  df <- load_table(a$table)  # load the table that was chosen
  pick_test(df[[a$resp]], df[[a$expl]])
})

result <- reactive({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  df <- load_table(a$table)
  tp <- analysis_type()
  validate(need(!is.na(tp), "No test matches this pair. Logistic regression needs a response with exactly two outcomes. Go back and choose different variables."))
  switch(tp,
         anova      = analyse_anova(df, yvar = a$resp, gvar = a$expl),
         regression = analyse_regression(df, yvar = a$resp, xvar = a$expl),
         chisq      = analyse_chisq(df, a$expl, a$resp),  # rows = explanatory, columns = response
         logistic   = analyse_logistic(df, yvar = a$resp, xvar = a$expl))
})

  # [Top bar and results body] =======================================================================================================================
  # output$results_ui    the top bar (Back on the left; Learn More / Save PDF / Worksheet / Explore Data / Feedback on the right), built once per
  #                      analysis. "Save PDF" uses the browser's print window - choose "Save as PDF" as the printer.
  # output$results_body  everything under the top bar. result() is calculated once and shared with the plots; r = the named list returned by the
  #                      matching analyse_* function. The "View More on Test" drop-down is a button that toggles the "open" class (see CSS). When
  #                      printing, the section is always shown. diag_groups() [D9] lays out the diagnostic plots.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$results_ui <- renderUI({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  div(class = "panel-card results-page",
      div(class = "results-bar no-print",
          actionButton("btn_results_back", "\u2190 Back to Data", class = "btn-te btn-outline"),
          div(class = "spacer"),
          actionButton("btn_learn", "Learn More", class = "btn-te btn-cyan"),
          tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-te", onclick = "window.print();", "Save PDF"),
          actionButton("btn_worksheet", NULL, icon = icon("microscope"), class = "btn-te btn-round has-tip", disabled = !WORKSHEET_ENABLED,
                       `data-tip` = "Download Worksheet", `aria-label` = "Download Worksheet"),  # opens the Worksheet window [F13]
          actionButton("btn_explore", NULL, icon = icon("table"), class = "btn-te btn-round has-tip",
                       `data-tip` = "Explore and download data", `aria-label` = "Explore and download data"),  # opens the Explore Data window [F11]
          actionButton("btn_feedback", NULL, icon = icon("comment-dots"), class = "btn-te btn-round has-tip",
                       `data-tip` = "Give feedback on this app", `aria-label` = "Give feedback on this app")),  # opens the Feedback window [F10]
      p(class = "hint", paste("Table:", pretty_name(a$table), "\u00b7 Response (y):", var_label(a$resp), "\u00b7 Explanatory (x):", var_label(a$expl))),
      uiOutput("results_body"))
})

output$results_body <- renderUI({
  r <- result()
  div(
    h2(r$title),
    h3(class = "sec-title", "Graphical Summary"),
    plot_box("res_plot", width = paste0(PLOT_W, "px"), height = paste0(plot_height(r), "px")),
    h3(class = "sec-title", "Numerical Summary"),
    div(class = "csv-tables", r$summary_ui),  # csv-tables shows each table's CSV button (see [B7])
    div(class = "more",
        tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-te more-toggle no-print",
                    onclick = "this.parentNode.classList.toggle('open');", "View More on Test \u25be"),
        div(class = "more-body",
            h3(class = "sec-title", paste("About the Test:", test_info[[r$type]]$name)),
            info_ui(r$type),
            h3(class = "sec-title", "Test Results"), r$test_ui,
            h3(class = "sec-title", "Diagnostics"),
            diag_groups(r),
            r$diag_ui)))
})

  # [Plots] ==========================================================================================================================================
  # Plots have fixed sizes in pixels (PLOT_W, DIAG_W, DIAG_H [D9]), so they look the same on every screen. suspendWhenHidden = FALSE draws the plots
  # before the drop-down is opened or the page is printed. Up to four diagnostic plots (regression with its log refit) are created in a loop; local()
  # gives each pass its own copy of i. req() skips the slots a test does not use.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
output$res_plot <- renderPlot(result()$main_plot, width = PLOT_W, height = function() plot_height(result()), res = PLOT_RES)
outputOptions(output, "res_plot", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
for (i in 1:4) local({
  ii <- i; id <- paste0("diag_plot_", ii)
  output[[id]] <- renderPlot({ r <- result(); req(length(r$diag_plots) >= ii); r$diag_plots[[ii]] },
                             width = DIAG_W, height = DIAG_H, res = PLOT_RES)
  outputOptions(output, id, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
})

  # [Graph downloads] ================================================================================================================================
  # plot_downloads() gives one graph its PDF and PNG download (the links in plot_box()). ggsave() redraws the same ggplot at the same size in inches
  # as on the page (pixels / PLOT_RES), so the file looks like what the student sees; PNGs are 300 dpi so they stay sharp in Word. cairo_pdf keeps
  # symbols such as the plus-minus sign intact. w and h are functions, because the chi-squared graph's height depends on the data. Files are named
  # after the test, e.g. "ANOVA_pH_by_Site_graph.png".
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
plot_downloads <- function(id, get_plot, w, h, label) {
  for (ext in c("pdf", "png")) local({
    e <- ext
    output[[paste0(id, "_", e)]] <- downloadHandler(
      filename = function() paste0(str_replace_all(result()$title, "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"), "_", label, ".", e),
      content  = function(file) ggsave(file, get_plot(), width = w() / PLOT_RES, height = h() / PLOT_RES, units = "in", dpi = 300,
                                       device = if (e == "pdf") grDevices::cairo_pdf else "png"))
    outputOptions(output, paste0(id, "_", e), suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)  # links work even inside the closed drop-down
  })
}
plot_downloads("res_plot", function() result()$main_plot, function() PLOT_W, function() plot_height(result()), "graph")
for (i in 1:4) local({
  ii <- i; id <- paste0("diag_plot_", ii)
  plot_downloads(id, function() result()$diag_plots[[ii]], function() DIAG_W, function() DIAG_H, paste0("diagnostic_", ii))
})

  # [F9. Learn More window] ==========================================================================================================================
  # A broad guide to the statistics in the app (based on the BYU-I class notes): choosing a test, how a hypothesis test works, reading the graphs,
  # checking assumptions, the four tests in one paragraph each (their `purpose` from test_info), and links to the class notes. The details for one
  # test (equations, hypotheses, assumptions) live under "View More on Test" on the results page.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
LEARN_LINKS <- c(
  "Making Inference (p-values and significance)" = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/MakingInference.html",
  "ANOVA"                                        = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/ANOVA.html",
  "Kruskal-Wallis Test"                          = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/Kruskal.html",
  "Linear Regression"                            = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/LinearRegression.html",
  "Logistic Regression"                          = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/LogisticRegression.html",
  "Chi-squared Tests"                            = "https://byuistats.github.io/Statistics-Notebook/ChiSquaredTests.html",
  "Checking Assumptions (Math 326)"              = "https://byuistats.github.io/Math326_Quarto4/assumptions.html")

observeEvent(input$btn_learn, {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = "Learn More: Statistics in This App", size = "l", easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Close"),
    div(class = "learn",
      h4(class = "sec-title", "1. Which Test?"),
      p("The app picks the test from the types of the two variables you choose. Quantitative variables are numbers (pH, temperature); qualitative variables are categories (soil type, Yes / No)."),
      tags$table(class = "te-table",
        tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Response (y)"), tags$th("Explanatory (x)"), tags$th("Test used"))),
        tags$tbody(
          tags$tr(tags$td("Quantitative"), tags$td("Qualitative"), tags$td(test_info$anova$name)),
          tags$tr(tags$td("Quantitative"), tags$td("Quantitative"), tags$td(test_info$regression$name)),
          tags$tr(tags$td("Qualitative"), tags$td("Qualitative"), tags$td(test_info$chisq$name)),
          tags$tr(tags$td("Qualitative with two outcomes (Yes / No)"), tags$td("Quantitative"), tags$td(test_info$logistic$name)))),
      h4(class = "sec-title", "2. How a Hypothesis Test Works"),
      tags$ul(
        tags$li(tags$strong("Hypotheses: "), "the null hypothesis (H₀) is the “nothing is going on” claim: no difference between groups, no relationship. The alternative hypothesis (Hₐ) is what we conclude if the data give strong evidence against H₀."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Test statistic: "), "one number (F, t, or χ²) that measures how far the data are from what H₀ predicts."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("p-value: "), "the probability of getting results as extreme as ours, or more extreme, if H₀ were true. A small p-value means our data would be surprising if nothing were going on."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Significance level (α = 0.05): "), "every test in this app uses 0.05. If p < 0.05, we reject H₀ (the result is statistically significant). If p ≥ 0.05, we fail to reject H₀, which is not the same as proving H₀ true."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Evidence, not proof: "), "even a significant result can be wrong. Rejecting H₀ when it is actually true is a Type I error, and α is the chance of making one. A relationship in observational data also does not prove that one variable causes the other.")),
      h4(class = "sec-title", "3. Reading the Graphs"),
      tags$ul(
        tags$li(tags$strong("Boxplot (ANOVA): "), "the box holds the middle 50% of the values, the line inside is the median, and the faint dots are the individual values. Compare the boxes side by side."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Scatterplot (Linear Regression): "), "each dot is one row of data and the line is the fitted line. A steeper line means a stronger change in y as x increases."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Bar chart (Chi-squared): "), "each panel counts the response in one group of the explanatory variable. If the bars have a different shape from panel to panel, the variables may be associated."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("S-curve (Logistic Regression): "), "the dots sit at 1 (the outcome happened) or 0 (it did not); the curve is the predicted chance of the outcome, and the dotted line marks a 50% chance.")),
      h4(class = "sec-title", "4. Checking Assumptions"),
      p("Every test rests on a few assumptions. If they are badly broken, the p-value can be misleading, so the app checks them for you under View More on Test:"),
      tags$ul(
        tags$li(tags$strong("Normal Q-Q plot: "), "compares the residuals (what the model misses) with a bell-shaped normal curve. The points should follow the line and stay inside the shaded band; the app flags the check if more than 10% fall outside."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Residuals vs. fitted plot: "), "the points should form an even, patternless cloud around 0. A funnel (megaphone) shape means the spread is not constant; a curve means a straight line does not fit."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Levene's test: "), "tests whether the groups have the same spread. Its H₀ is equal spread, so a p-value above 0.05 is what we want."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("Independence: "), "each row should not influence another. No plot can check this; it depends on how the data were collected."),
        tags$li(tags$strong("When a check fails: "), "ANOVA adds the Kruskal-Wallis test, regression refits the model with log(y), chi-squared adds a simulation-based p-value, and logistic regression warns you about a poor fit.")),
      h4(class = "sec-title", "5. The Four Tests at a Glance"),
      lapply(names(test_info), function(k) p(tags$strong(test_info[[k]]$name, ": "), test_info[[k]]$purpose)),
      p(class = "note", "For the equations, hypotheses, and assumption checks of the test you ran, open View More on Test on the results page."),
      h4(class = "sec-title", "6. Want More?"),
      p("These BYU-Idaho class notes go deeper into each topic:"),
      tags$ul(lapply(names(LEARN_LINKS), function(n) tags$li(tags$a(href = LEARN_LINKS[[n]], target = "_blank", n)))))))
})

  # [F10. Feedback window] ===========================================================================================================================
  # The round speech-bubble button asks whether the visitor wants to give feedback. "Yes" opens FEEDBACK_URL [D1] in a new browser tab and closes the
  # window; "No" just closes it. Both buttons close the window in the browser (data-dismiss), so R does not need to react to them.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$btn_feedback, {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = "Feedback", size = "s", easyClose = TRUE,
    p("Would you like to give feedback on this app?"),
    footer = tagList(
      modalButton("No"),
      tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-te", `data-dismiss` = "modal", `data-bs-dismiss` = "modal",
                  onclick = sprintf("window.open('%s', '_blank', 'noopener');", FEEDBACK_URL), "Yes"))))
})

  # [F11. Explore Data window and downloads] =========================================================================================================
  # The round data-table button asks which version of the analysed table to download:
  #   Clean  the table the app uses (from Data/), saved as an Excel file (.xlsx).
  #   Raw    the original Tiny Earth export (from Data_Raw/), unchanged. Raw files are named with hyphens ("aa-screen-isolates.xlsx"). A Combined
  #          table has no raw file of its own, so its main table's raw file is given.
  # Clicking either choice starts the download and closes the window (removeModal() via input$dl_done).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
raw_path <- function(key) file.path("Data_Raw", paste0(str_replace_all(str_remove(key, "_combined$"), "_", "-"), ".xlsx"))

observeEvent(input$btn_explore, {
  key <- req(rv$analysis)$table
  has_raw <- file.exists(raw_path(key))
  done <- "Shiny.setInputValue('dl_done', Math.random());"
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = tagList(icon("table"), " Explore Data"), easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Cancel"),
    p("Download the data behind this analysis: ", tags$strong(paste0(pretty_name(key), if (str_detect(key, "_combined$")) " (Combined)" else " (Individual)")), "."),
    div(class = "dl-choices",
        downloadLink("dl_clean", class = "dl-choice", onclick = done,
                     tags$strong(icon("broom"), " Clean Data"),
                     span("The tidied table this app analyses (.xlsx).")),
        if (has_raw)
          downloadLink("dl_raw", class = "dl-choice", onclick = done,
                       tags$strong(icon("file-excel"), " Raw Data"),
                       span(if (str_detect(key, "_combined$")) "The original Tiny Earth export of the main table, before cleaning or joining (.xlsx)."
                            else "The original Tiny Earth export, before any cleaning (.xlsx)."))
        else div(class = "dl-choice", tags$strong(icon("file-excel"), " Raw Data"), span("No raw file was found for this table.")))))
})
observeEvent(input$dl_done, removeModal())

output$dl_clean <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() paste0(req(rv$analysis)$table, "_clean.xlsx"),
  content  = function(file) writexl::write_xlsx(load_table(req(rv$analysis)$table), file))
output$dl_raw <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() basename(raw_path(req(rv$analysis)$table)),
  content  = function(file) file.copy(raw_path(req(rv$analysis)$table), file))
outputOptions(output, "dl_clean", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
outputOptions(output, "dl_raw",   suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

  # [F12. Debug windows (only when DEBUG_MODE is TRUE)] ==============================================================================================
  # The Debug button lists one link per test in DEBUG_CASES [D1]; each opens the app in a new window with ?debug=<test> in its address. When a window
  # starts with that address, the observer below fills in rv$analysis from DEBUG_CASES and jumps straight to the results page.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
debug_js <- function(test) sprintf("window.open('?debug=%s', 'te_debug_%s', 'popup,width=1150,height=900');", test, test)

observeEvent(input$btn_debug, {
  req(DEBUG_MODE)
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = tagList(icon("bug"), " Debug: open each test"), easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Close"),
    p("Each link opens that test's results page in a new window, using the variables set in DEBUG_CASES."),
    tags$ul(lapply(names(DEBUG_CASES), function(k) {
      cs <- DEBUG_CASES[[k]]
      tags$li(tags$a(href = "#", onclick = paste(debug_js(k), "return false;"), tags$strong(test_info[[k]]$name)),
              sprintf(" — %s: %s by %s", pretty_name(cs$table), var_label(cs$resp), var_label(cs$expl)))
    }))))
})

observeEvent(session$clientData$url_search, {
  test <- parseQueryString(session$clientData$url_search)$debug
  req(DEBUG_MODE, !is.null(test), test %in% names(DEBUG_CASES))
  rv$table    <- DEBUG_CASES[[test]]$table
  rv$analysis <- DEBUG_CASES[[test]]
  rv$page     <- "results"
}, once = TRUE)

  # [F13. Worksheet window (only when WORKSHEET_ENABLED is TRUE)] ====================================================================================
  # The microscope button first asks "Would you like to download an analysis worksheet?". Yes swaps in a second window offering the Word and PDF
  # versions for the test on the page (ws_path() builds e.g. "Worksheets/anova_worksheet.docx"); a format whose file is missing is shown as not yet
  # available. Choosing a file starts the download and closes the window (input$dl_done, as in [F11]).
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
ws_path <- function(ext) file.path(WORKSHEET_DIR, paste0(result()$type, "_worksheet.", ext))

observeEvent(input$btn_worksheet, {
  req(WORKSHEET_ENABLED)
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = tagList(icon("microscope"), " Download Worksheet"), easyClose = TRUE,
    p("Would you like to download an analysis worksheet?"),
    footer = tagList(modalButton("No"), actionButton("ws_yes", "Yes", class = "btn-te"))))
})
observeEvent(input$ws_yes, {
  done   <- "Shiny.setInputValue('dl_done', Math.random());"
  choice <- function(id, ext, label, ico)
    if (file.exists(ws_path(ext))) downloadLink(id, class = "dl-choice", onclick = done, tags$strong(icon(ico), " ", label), span(paste0(".", ext)))
    else div(class = "dl-choice", tags$strong(icon(ico), " ", label), span("Not available yet."))
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = tagList(icon("microscope"), " Download Worksheet"), easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Cancel"),
    p("Choose a format for the ", tags$strong(test_info[[result()$type]]$name), " worksheet:"),
    div(class = "dl-choices", choice("dl_ws_docx", "docx", "Word Document", "file-word"), choice("dl_ws_pdf", "pdf", "PDF", "file-pdf"))))
})
for (ext in c("docx", "pdf")) local({
  e <- ext
  output[[paste0("dl_ws_", e)]] <- downloadHandler(filename = function() basename(ws_path(e)),
                                                   content  = function(file) file.copy(ws_path(e), file))
  outputOptions(output, paste0("dl_ws_", e), suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
})
```
